articles.titulo: Temperature-dependent bloodmeal retention is associated with altered midgut ROS homeostasis in Aedes aegypti.
articles.autores: Ferreira PG, Profeta CA, … Mendes TAO (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Temperature is a key environmental factor influencing mosquito physiology and vector competence, yet the mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. Previous transcriptomic analyses of the midgut of Aedes aegypti maintained at different temperatures revealed differential expression of genes associated with blood digestion. Here, we investigated whether these transcriptional changes are accompanied by alterations in digestive enzyme activity, bloodmeal digestion kinetics, bloodmeal retention and midgut reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis. Mosquitoes maintained at 20°C exhibited delayed bloodmeal digestion and prolonged bloodmeal retention compared with those maintained at 28 and 36°C. Delayed bloodmeal digestion at 20°C was accompanied by sustained accumulation of soluble peroxides and nitric oxide, together with increased expression of antioxidant genes, indicating prolonged, temperature-dependent oxidative stress in the mosquito midgut. These findings suggest that cooler temperatures extend bloodmeal retention and prolong oxidative stress in the midgut, providing a physiological link between environmental temperature, digestive dynamics and redox homeostasis that may ultimately influence vector competence.

v6.implicacao: Alimentação sanguínea de Aedes / Imunometabolismo: a janela de retenção do repasto e a redox do intestino médio dependem da temperatura, então a temperatura precisa entrar como covariável nos ensaios de repasto HFHS e de competência vetorial.
v6.resumo: Em Aedes aegypti mantidas a 20, 28 e 36 °C, a 20 °C a digestão do repasto é mais lenta e o sangue fica retido por mais tempo no intestino médio, com acúmulo sustentado de peróxidos solúveis e óxido nítrico e maior expressão de genes antioxidantes.

articles.titulo: Evolutionary Events Underlying Vector Competence and Epidemiological Variation in Hematophagous Diptera with Special Reference to Sand Flies and Mosquitoes.
articles.autores: Sinha S, Pandey R, … Mishra N (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Order Diptera includes house flies, blow flies, horse flies, midges, mosquitoes, sand flies, etc. Among these, mosquitoes and sand flies play a central role in the transmission of diseases affecting man and animals. They are typically characterised by a single pair of functional wings and a reduced, modified pair of halteres. Dipterans have evolved over 200 million years, undergoing extensive diversification shaped by adaptations in flight, sensory biology, feeding behaviour, and life history traits. Hematophagy is independently evolved in mosquitoes and sand flies, has been a key trait linked to reproductive success, while also facilitating pathogen transmission.
The ability of this order of insects to transmit diseases/pathogens is referred as vector competence. It depends on complex interactions between vector genetics, microbiota, immune responses and environmental factors. It also involves multiple physiological barriers within the insect/vector. More than 150,000 species described are distributed across numerous genera and evolutionary lineages. Dipterans have well-defined synapomorphies, which include specialised mouthparts and complete metamorphosis, which have helped them to exploit diverse ecological niches.
Understanding their evolutionary history and important biological traits underlying vector competence is crucial for explaining why only certain species efficiently transmit pathogens, parasites, bacteria and viruses. This kind of knowledge is crucial for improving vector surveillance, designing new control strategies, and targeted intervention for reducing the global burden of vector-borne diseases. Although many arthropods can carry pathogens incidentally, a limited number of these hematophagous insects act as consistent and efficient disease vectors. Hence, play a crucial role in the epidemiology of vector-borne diseases.
Successful transmission of the pathogen depends predominantly on vector competence. This reflects the genetic compatibility between the pathogen and the arthropod vector, as most ingested pathogens are killed during blood meal digestion. The broader concept of vectorial capacity and vectorial competence is shaped largely by complex interactions with the vector, host, pathogen, environment, and the arthropod-associated microbiota. This significantly influences host morphology and transmission efficiency. Notably, vectorial capacity is not a static phenomenon; it varies across time and space, thereby altering host-pathogen transmission dynamics/cycles. Feeding behaviour is attributed to transmission dynamics, like anthropophilic mosquitoes, e.g. Aedes spp. exhibit more susceptibility to viral infections as they predominantly feed on humans. Hematophagy/blood feeding occurs at different life stages across insect/vector taxa, with only female mosquitoes now requiring blood meals. In addition to blood, mosquitoes also rely heavily on plant sap sugars for survival. Contemporary climate change and biological invasions are expanding vector distributions. Thus, increasing disease risk in previously unaffected areas/populations, underscoring the critical need for a deeper understanding of the triad of vector-pathogen-environment interactions. This review addresses this triad and the evolution of this character in dipterans.

v6.resumo: Revisão sobre a evolução da hematofagia e dos traços de competência vetorial em dípteros, sem dados novos.

articles.titulo: Inflammation-driven epigenetic memory in infertility and chronic endometritis.
articles.autores: Chen R, Diao L, … Arck PC (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chronic endometritis (CE) is a persistent, low-grade inflammatory condition of the endometrium, typically caused by microbial infections. CE is often asymptomatic, leading to frequent underdiagnosis. It is frequently identified during the assessment of causes for infertility. Even after resolving the infectious etiology by antibiotic treatment, infertility persists in a number of patients. Emerging evidence from chronic inflammatory diseases affecting epithelial tissues, e.g., in the gut, suggests that inflammatory conditions can induce long-lasting epigenetic changes, e.g., in innate immune cells. Notably, tissues outside the immune system can also retain memory of inflammatory events and environmental insults via epigenetic modifications. This review summarizes how epigenetic changes can affect endometrial function, drawing on current knowledge of CE. It also discusses how inflammation prompts these changes. We propose that persistent epigenetic memory in both immune and non-immune endometrial cells plays a crucial role in sustaining CE-associated adversities, such as infertility. Future research should focus on pinpointing specific epigenetic patterns in CE and exploring how inflammation-induced memory leads to cellular dysfunction in the endometrium. Understanding these mechanisms will advance CE diagnosis and open doors to new treatment options for infertility, focusing on reversing the inflammatory memory retained upon treatment of CE.

v6.resumo: Revisão de memória epigenética inflamatória na endometrite crônica, em células imunes e não imunes.

articles.titulo: Immunometabolic Memory in Obesity: Nutritional Drivers, Persistence, and Reversibility.
articles.autores: Reytor-González C, Zambrano-Villacres R, … Simancas-Racines D (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Obesity reshapes immune function across adipose tissue, circulation, and hematopoietic compartments. Weight reduction improves cardiometabolic health, yet emerging evidence indicates that prior obesity can leave persistent cellular, transcriptional, and epigenetic changes. Whether nutrition can reverse this biological imprint remains uncertain. We conducted a critical narrative review informed by structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, the Cochrane Library, and Epistemonikos, complemented by backward and forward citation tracking. We prioritized mechanistic human studies, controlled dietary interventions, longitudinal weight-loss studies, and experiments that tested persistence after stimulus withdrawal or response to re-exposure. Evidence was interpreted according to biological compartment and study design rather than pooled statistically. Obesogenic exposures can alter innate immune metabolism, inflammasome signaling, hematopoiesis, and chromatin states. Animal studies provide the strongest evidence that these changes can persist after weight normalization and amplify responses during weight regain. Human studies show incomplete normalization of adipose immune states, persistent adipocyte programs, and durable methylation changes in T lymphocytes after weight loss. Dietary interventions can lower inflammatory tone and modify immune metabolism, microbial metabolites, and lipid mediator pathways, but no dietary pattern has been shown to erase established obesity-associated immune memory in humans. An evidence map built on a core set of 47 studies showed that experimental work dominates the induction, persistence and re-challenge domains, whereas human evidence clusters in post-weight-loss remodelling and dietary modulation; human re-challenge data were absent and no study provided a direct test of reversal in humans. Obesity-associated immunometabolic memory appears to be distributed across hematopoietic, immune, adipose, stromal, and microbial compartments. Nutrition can modulate mechanisms implicated in this persistence, but human evidence of reversal is lacking, and whether pharmacologically induced weight loss leaves a comparable imprint has not been tested. Mechanistic trials should separate energy deficit, diet composition, adiposity change, and weight-loss modality and include a weight-stable follow-up and functional re-challenge where feasible.

articles.titulo: Trained Immunity and Persistent Myeloid Responsiveness in MASH.
articles.autores: Fu L, Guo R, … Zhang Q (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) involves hepatocellular injury, myeloid activation, and fibrotic remodeling that may resolve unevenly following metabolic improvement. Whether previous injury leaves a functionally consequential innate immune imprint remains unresolved. This review evaluates trained immunity as a candidate mechanism linking exposure history to persistent hepatic myeloid responsiveness. We distinguish continued activation by lipotoxic and stromal signals from responses retained after stimulus withdrawal, macrophage replacement, and hematopoietic progenitor programming. Evidence from Kupffer cells, monocyte-derived macrophages, and lipid- or scar-associated populations reveals divergent inflammatory, efferocytosis, and matrix remodeling functions. Receptor-dependent lipid handling intersects with glycolysis, citrate-derived acetyl-CoA, serine and one-carbon metabolism, NAD+ availability and histone methylation, acetylation, and lactylation. These pathways explain how metabolic inputs regulate inflammatory competence, but their alteration during active MASH does not establish immune memory. Rested monocyte training models provide stronger temporal evidence than most disease-specific studies, whereas protective TREM2-dependent responses caution against indiscriminate suppression of disease-associated macrophages. Establishing a contribution to MASH recurrence requires lineage-resolved investigations spanning injury, regression, and rechallenge, with interventions separating memory establishment, maintenance, and effector output. If exposure-dependent myeloid memory contributes causally to MASH recurrence, targeting maladaptive responsiveness could complement injury control while preserving hepatic repair.

articles.titulo: Variation in the composition of nutrients in the blood of vertebrate hosts affect gonotrophic cycle velocity and the reproductive output of Culex pipiens.
articles.autores: Yassin MT, El Kholy S, … Seif A (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Deep understanding of vector biology is essential for improving disease control strategies. Most female mosquitoes are anautogenous, requiring a blood meal from vertebrate host for egg development. However, the impact of host blood nutritional composition such as red and white blood cell counts, hemoglobin percentage, total protein, and free amino acids on the gonotrophic cycle remains unclear. In this study, female Culex pipiens were allowed to feed on 4 vertebrate hosts (pigeon, chicken, mice, and human), and the nutritional profiles of the blood meals were quantified. Results revealed that avian blood meals contained higher levels of free amino acids compared to mammalian blood. Females fed on avian hosts exhibited a significantly shorter gonotrophic cycle and enhanced ovarian development. These findings suggest that variation in blood nutritional composition may influence reproductive timing in Cx. pipiens and could contribute to host-associated differences in feeding preference.

articles.titulo: Improved long-read sequencing technology reveals full genome architecture of Malian Plasmodium falciparum field isolates
articles.autores: Autores não informados
articles.resumo_original: Understanding genome plasticity in malaria parasites and the diversity of their repetitive gene families requires high-quality reference genomes derived from parasites recently isolated from patients. However, generating such genomes in Plasmodium falciparum remains challenging owing to the parasite's extreme AT content, extensive repetitive regions, and the frequent occurrence of multiclonal infections in endemic settings. As a result, most available reference genomes are derived from laboratory-adapted strains, that have experienced prolonged in vitro maintenance, and that incompletely represent natural parasite diversity. We developed and optimized a de novo assembly strategy based on PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and applied it to eight recently-isolated and cloned P. falciparum parasites from Mali. HiFi sequencing enabled highly accurate genome reconstruction, yielding assemblies with a mean of 18 contigs, 301 pseudogenes, and a frameshift rate of 0.04% following Liftoff annotation. Assemblies showed high structural integrity and near-complete chromosomes, including improved recovery of subtelomeric regions and multigene families, without requiring short-read correction. Despite overall conservation of chromosome organization, substantial variation was observed in chromosome-end architecture, subtelomeric structure, and telomeric repeat content among parasite genomes. Our approach simplifies the generation of high-quality P. falciparum genomes and reduces sequencing requirements fourfold. The resulting assemblies enabled characterization of natural variation in telomere plasticity and multicopy gene family diversity in field isolates. These findings establish PacBio HiFi sequencing as an effective and scalable strategy for producing highly contiguous and accurate de novo assemblies of P. falciparum, supporting the development of geographically-diverse, field-relevant malaria parasite reference genomes.

v6.resumo: Preprint: sequenciamento de leitura longa revela a arquitetura genômica completa de Plasmodium maliano. Só título e bloco lidos.

articles.titulo: Parasite-induced ER-PVM contacts promote CERT-dependent ceramide delivery to the apicomplexan vacuole
articles.autores: Autores não informados
articles.resumo_original: Apicomplexan parasites rely on host lipids for replication, yet how host transport machinery is coupled to the parasitophorous vacuole membrane (PVM) remains unresolved. Here, we uncover a host-parasite membrane contact site mechanism driving ceramide delivery to the vacuole. Host ceramide transfer protein (CERT) targets the PVM via its PH domain, cooperating with host VAP-B to promote sphingolipid accumulation and support Toxoplasma and Plasmodium development. By combining VAP-B proximity labeling with FFAT motif predictions, we identified TgVPS13 as a parasite-encoded FFAT effector that physically engages host VAP-B at the host-parasite interface. Conditional depletion of TgVPS13 markedly reduces vacuolar sphingolipid enrichment, partially impairs host CERT recruitment at the PVM, disrupts intravacuolar parasite organization, and severely restricts replication. Together, these findings establish a model in which TgVPS13-VAP-B tethering creates ER-PVM proximity, organizing a functional contact site that optimizes CERT-mediated ceramide transfer for efficient host lipid acquisition.

v6.resumo: Preprint: contatos RE-membrana do vacúolo parasitóforo induzidos pelo parasito promovem entrega de ceramida dependente de CERT ao apicomplexo. Só título lido.

articles.titulo: Urbanization development characteristics coincide with elevated Anopheles stephensi habitat suitability.
articles.autores: Sun Y, Liu W, … Liu Q (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The invasion of Anopheles stephensi into Africa is increasing risks in urban areas, posing challenges to global malaria elimination. Unlike most malaria vectors, Anopheles stephensi is well adapted to urban environments, thereby imposing a substantial burden on urban malaria transmission. Here, we quantify the influence of urbanization on Anopheles stephensi habitat suitability and examine potential underlying mechanisms. Habitat suitability increases along the urbanization gradient, with the highest suitability observed in high-density urban regions. Urbanization increases the habitat suitability, particularly in Africa, with the transition from urban to high-density urban areas showing the greatest increase in suitability. Moreover, we identify construction-related activities as a key pathway linking urbanization to habitat suitability, consistent with the proliferation of artificial larval habitats in built environments. These findings provide a mechanistic understanding of urban-associated risk, inform large-scale malaria predictions to support the integration of vector surveillance with urban planning.

v6.resumo: Modelo de adequabilidade de habitat de Anopheles stephensi ao longo do gradiente de urbanização; atividades de construção ligam urbanização a criadouros artificiais.

articles.titulo: Spatial and Spatiotemporal Clustering of Dengue in Jambi Municipality, Indonesia, 2010-2024.
articles.autores: Syukri M, Salim M, … Billardi A (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue is a public health problem in Indonesia, particularly in urbanising cities where transmission patterns are spatially heterogeneous and seasonally dynamic. This study aimed to identify the spatial and spatiotemporal clusters of dengue cases in Jambi Municipality, Indonesia. A retrospective ecological study was conducted using dengue surveillance data aggregated across 62 urban villages.
Monthly counts of clinically diagnosed dengue cases reported through routine surveillance between 1 January 2010 and 31 December 2024 were obtained from the Jambi Municipality Health Office. Population data were obtained from the Central Bureau of Statistics and cases were analysed at the urban-village level to support local surveillance. Retrospective spatial and space-time cluster analyses were carried out using SaTScan TM with a discrete Poisson model. Monte Carlo hypothesis testing was used to assess statistical significance, and the clusters were visualised with Quantum GIS.
A total of 7,099 clinically diagnosed dengue cases were reported. Purely spatial and space-time analyses identified 24 and 39 significant clusters, respectively. Recurrent high-risk clusters were concentrated mainly in the central and southern parts of the municipality, although their locations varied by year. Among the 39 space-time clusters, 37 were in a minimum of one rainy-season month (October-April), and the other two secondary clusters were limited to the dry season (August 2011 and June 2023.
Dengue showed recurrent small-area clustering and significant overlap with rainy-season months over 15 years, suggesting the need for fine-scale surveillance and spatially targeted vector control.

articles.titulo: Genomic epidemiology of CHIKV during the largest outbreak in Mainland China - implication for CHIKV intervention.
articles.autores: Yi L, Xiang S, … Lu J (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has caused recurrent epidemics across tropical and subtropical regions globally. In 2025, Guangdong, China, experienced the largest documented CHIKV outbreak in mainland China, with 23,464 reported cases across all 21 prefecture-level cities. We conducted integrated epidemiological, genomic, and phylodynamic analyses to investigate the outbreak's origins, transmission dynamics, and CHIKV lineage evolution. The Guangdong strain belongs to the East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype, Middle African lineage (ECSA-MAL) - one of several CHIKV lineages co-circulating globally in 2025; a long internal branch separates ECSA-MAL from previously sequenced relatives, indicating substantial surveillance gaps in endemic regions. Phylodynamic analysis using a local molecular clock model estimated that the viral introduction occurred within a narrow window in early April 2025 (95% HPD: March 26-April 12), suggesting a 2.5-month period of cryptic transmission prior to detection. The prolonged silent phase aligns with vector dynamics: the Mosquito Ovitrap Index in the outbreak town of Beijiao, Foshan, stayed low in April (3.0) before surging to 9.0 through July - consistent with suppressed early transmission followed by seasonal amplification. Human migration from the two epidemic epicenters was moderately associated with the spatial distribution of cases (Spearman ρ around 0.5), while mosquito ecology may constrain spatial spread. Phylowave analysis on global circulating strains identified 33 lineage-defining mutations across 14 sublineages, concentrated in NSP3, E1 and E2. Four of these have been experimentally validated as adaptive mutations. This study demonstrates the critical need for enhanced genomic surveillance during pre-peak months and underscores the importance of monitoring adaptive mutations across diverse ecological regions.

v6.resumo: Epidemiologia genômica de CHIKV no maior surto da China continental.

articles.titulo: Systemic cytokine profiling reveals distinct pro-inflammatory signatures of arboviruses infections.
articles.autores: Sarmento IV, Fantecelle CH, … Gomes DCO (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Arboviruses are a growing public health concern in tropical regions, where dengue virus (DENV), chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and oropouche virus (OROV) frequently co-circulate and cause overlapping clinical manifestations. In this study, we characterised the systemic inflammatory response by quantifying 12 cytokines and chemokines using a multiplex immunoassay in 163 patients with laboratory-confirmed acute arboviral infection: DENV1 (n = 28) and DENV2 (n = 39) patients without warning signs, CHIKV (n = 42) and OROV (n = 54). Thirty-one healthy controls (HC, n = 31) were also included. Clinically, arthralgia was the only feature that reliably distinguished the infections, occurring in 57.1% of CHIKV patients compared with 7.4-30.8% in the other groups, whereas fever, headache and myalgia overlapped substantially across all four. Immunologically, OROV induced a selective response with elevated IL-18 and CCL2/MCP-1 alongside reduced IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-12p70, IL-23 and IL-17 A; DENV1 and DENV2 elicited broad activation of pro-inflammatory and antiviral mediators, with DENV1 engaging a wider range of cytokines than DENV2; and CHIKV elevated IFN-α2, IFN-γ, IL-18, IL-6, IL-8, MCP-1 and IL-17 A. Cytokine network analysis revealed virus-specific patterns of immune connectivity, with OROV showing the most coordinated cytokines and chemokine response and CHIKV the most fragmented. Circulating cytokine concentrations were largely independent of viral load across all viruses, indicating that systemic inflammation during acute arboviral infection is driven primarily by host immune activation rather than by viral replication kinetics. These findings establish distinct immunological signatures for DENV, CHIKV, and OROV that may support differential diagnosis and inform the development of pathogen-specific therapeutic strategies.

v6.resumo: Perfil de 12 citocinas em 163 pacientes com DENV1, DENV2, CHIKV e OROV: o OROV tem resposta seletiva (IL-18 e CCL2 altas, IL-1β e TNF-α baixas) e as citocinas independem da carga viral.

articles.titulo: Synergistic Anti-Zika Activity of Repurposed Statin and Clofibrate Combinations: Evidence from Oleic Acid-Mediated Metabolic Complementation.
articles.autores: Lee CD, Park SI, … Park JG (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) substantially relies on host lipid metabolism, presenting a prime target for host-directed antivirals. To identify host-directed antiviral interventions while circumventing interferon-mediated transcriptomic masking, we curated a dual-virus (dengue and ZIKV) gene signature to query the Connectivity Map. Top lipid-lowering candidates were validated using a reporter virus (rZIKV-Venus) and an authentic wild-type (WT) ZIKV in Vero E6 cells-a model deliberately selected for its interferon deficiency to isolate pure metabolic responses. Dose-response screening of 67 prioritized compounds identified atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, and clofibrate as potent ZIKV inhibitors. Statin-clofibrate combinations exhibited strong synergy, with fractional inhibitory concentration index (FICI) values of 0.203 (atorvastatin-clofibrate) and 0.117 (rosuvastatin-clofibrate) for the 4:1 clofibrate-to-statin ratio and an optimized selectivity index. Mechanistically, exogenous oleic acid supplementation induced significant metabolic complementation, significantly restoring both host lipid droplet (LD) abundance and ZIKV replication readouts suppressed by the dual treatment. Relative LD intensity strongly correlated with viral intensity in both models (Pearson r = 0.951 and 0.956, respectively; both p < 0.0001). These findings demonstrate that concurrent pharmacological modulation of host lipid metabolism exerts synergistic anti-ZIKV effects, highlighting highly curated transcriptomic repurposing as a mechanistic prioritization strategy for host-directed antiviral discovery.

v6.resumo: Combinações de estatina e clofibrato reaproveitadas com atividade sinérgica anti-Zika in vitro.

articles.titulo: Identification of Arboviruses and Other Viral Signatures Using Entomo-Virological Surveillance in the Santa Marta District, Colombia.
articles.autores: Franco-Salazar JP, Quintero-Cortés P, … Usme-Ciro JA (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Current surveillance strategies for arboviral diseases involve serological and virological study of clinical cases and characterization of presence and densities of immature and mature stages of vectors. Our objective was to establish an entomo-virological surveillance of flaviviruses and alphaviruses in urban and rural areas of the Santa Marta district, Colombia.
Mosquitoes and sandfly specimens were collected using CO2-baited CDC light, Shannon traps, and entomological nets with aspirators. Specimens belonging to every morphotype were separated and stored for processing through classical taxonomy, molecular systematics, and for virus detection using generic, specific RT-PCR methods, and DNA sequencing. Sequences were aligned through MAFFT and phylogenetic trees reconstructed through IQ-TREE.
A total of 2953 specimens were collected. Several species of vectors were identified, with Ae. aegypti and Culex sp. being predominant in both urban and rural areas. Viral detection and sequencing revealed the circulation of genotype V (American/African) of Orthoflavivirus denguei (DENV) type 1, cocirculation of lineages 1V_D.1 and 1V_D.2 with different recent origins, and presumptive cryptic circulation of Orthoflavivirus zikaense (ZIKV) based on molecular detection without sequence confirmation. Alphavirus chikungunya (CHIKV) was not detected in the tested pools during the study period. In addition, the presence of Culex flavivirus and a putative nonretroviral integrated RNA virus (NIRV) element derived from a Menghai-like flavivirus was detected in the genome of Ae. aegypti.
This study demonstrated the circulation of DENV in the vector population and provided presumptive molecular evidence of ZIKV. In-depth analysis of flavivirus-positive samples allowed the detection of the Culex flavivirus, as well as a putative NIRV element in the genome of Ae. aegypti, whose effects on vector competence and arboviruses dynamics justify further research.

v6.resumo: Identificação de arbovírus e outras assinaturas virais por vigilância entomovirológica.

articles.titulo: Phosphorus limitation shifts cellular phosphorus allocation toward polyphosphate by depleting other phosphorus pools in Synechococcus.
articles.autores: Filella A, Segura-Noguera M, … Duhamel S (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Polyphosphate (polyP) is a ubiquitous and evolutionarily conserved form of phosphorus (P) present in all living organisms, yet its role in cellular and biogeochemical P cycling remains poorly constrained. In P-depleted marine environments, polyP consistently represents a larger fraction of total particulate P (TPP) than in P-replete environments, contradicting its classical role as a luxury storage compound. This unresolved discrepancy has been hypothesized to arise from reductions of other cellular P pools rather than by de novo polyP synthesis, but this has not been tested under steady-state conditions. Using continuous cultures of the globally important marine cyanobacterium Synechococcus sp. WH8102 grown across a gradient of phosphate availability, we address this knowledge gap. Although phosphate availability strongly affected growth rates, single-cell C:N:P stoichiometry and the expression of P-stress genes, polyP:TPP increased with decreasing phosphate availability, reproducing the pattern observed in oligotrophic oceans. This shift was not driven by de novo polyP synthesis; cellular polyP concentrations (polyP per biovolume) remained stable across growth rates (Kruskal-Wallis, P value = 0.06), whereas other intracellular P pools, including RNA, free intracellular phosphate, ATP, and phospholipids, were preferentially depleted with decreasing phosphate availability (2.6-11.8-fold across P pools), increasing the relative contribution of polyP to TPP. Expression of polyP metabolism genes showed minimal changes across treatments. These results indicate that P deficiency responses observed in oligotrophic environments and various microorganisms in batch culture reflect slow-growing physiology resulting in polyP maintenance and preferential depletion of more labile P pools, with consequences for interpreting particulate P stoichiometry and export.

articles.titulo: GM-CSF and M-CSF driven differentiation differentially regulates Chikungunya virus infection and antiviral responses in human monocyte-derived macrophages.
articles.autores: Veloz J, Zyulina V, … Fernandez-Sesma A (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chikungunya virus is an arthritogenic alphavirus causing debilitating joint pain in infected individuals. The mechanisms driving CHIKV-associated arthralgia is poorly understood, however, macrophages have been implicated as potential reservoirs of persistent viral material and mediators of immunopathology. Granulocyte Macrophage-Colony Stimulating Factor (GM-CSF) and Macrophage-Colony Stimulating Factor (M-CSF) are cytokines that serve as myeloid growth factors that bias macrophages toward pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory phenotypes, respectively. In this study, we examined how cytokine-driven macrophage differentiation via GM-CSF and M-CSF influences susceptibility to and responses against CHIKV infection in vitro. Using parallel donor-matched cultures of primary macrophages, we show that GM-CSF-differentiated macrophages are highly permissive to CHIKV and Mayaro virus (MAYV) infection and support robust viral replication, whereas M-CSF-differentiated macrophages are resistant to CHIKV replication and lack detectable levels of viral protein expression. Despite these differences, we observed pro-inflammatory, M1-skewing of CHIKV-infected macrophages, regardless of differentiation state. Interestingly, we observe higher production of IFNα and IP10/CXCL10 in M-CSF differentiated macrophages, suggesting that M-CSF promotes an antiviral state that restricts CHIKV infection. Stimulation of macrophages with double-stranded RNA (polyinosinic:polycytidylic acid; poly(I:C)), but not with single-stranded RNA (resiquimod, R848), recapitulated the antiviral cytokine and chemokine response induced by CHIKV infection. These findings suggest that dsRNA sensing plays a more prominent role than ssRNA sensing in driving the macrophage antiviral response to CHIKV. Together, these findings highlight macrophage differentiation as a critical determinant of CHIKV susceptibility and antiviral immunity in humans, with implications for understanding inflammatory pathogenesis during infection.

articles.titulo: No cross-resistance to cry toxins and strong fitness costs associated with Vip3Aa resistance in a chitin synthase knockout strain of Helicoverpa armigera.
articles.autores: Zhang M, Liu C, … He YZ (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Genetically modified crops expressing insecticidal proteins from Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) are widely planted to suppress pest populations, but the emergence of resistance in pests threatens their durability. The evolution of resistance is strongly shaped by cross-resistance patterns and associated fitness costs. Recent studies have linked loss-of-function mutations in the chitin synthase 2 (CHS2) gene with resistance to Vip3Aa in several lepidopteran pests, including the cotton bollworm Helicoverpa armigera. However, whether disruption of CHS2 confers cross-resistance to Cry toxins and imposes fitness costs in H. armigera remains unknown. Here, we examined the cross-resistance profile of a Vip3Aa-resistant H. armigera strain with CHS2 knocked out (CHS2-KO) and assessed its fitness costs when reared on wheat germ diet, cotton leaves, and corn ears lacking Vip3Aa.
The CHS2-KO strain exhibited >2852-fold recessive resistance to Vip3Aa but had no cross-resistance to Cry1Ac or Cry2Ab. When maintained on wheat germ diet without Vip3Aa, CHS2-KO had delayed development and lower larval survival, lower pupal weight, and reduced adult fecundity relative to the susceptible parental strain SCD. Survival of CHS2-KO larvae was 1% after 7 days on cotton leaves and 2% after 5 days on corn ears, indicating marked fitness costs. No peritrophic matrix was found in the midguts of CHS2-KO larvae. Midgut transcriptome profiling of CHS2-KO larvae revealed upregulation of transcripts involved in protein digestion, cellular absorption, and immune responses with a corresponding decline in transcripts involved in metabolism.
Vip3Aa resistance in H. armigera mediated by loss-of-function mutations in CHS2 is inherited as a recessive trait, lacks cross-resistance to Cry toxins, and incurs strong fitness costs. These findings suggest that complete loss of CHS2, as seen in the CHS2-KO strain, may be negatively selected in the absence of Vip3Aa. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.titulo: Lipid metabolic reprogramming in honey bee response to Hafnia alvei infection: insights from temporal transcriptome analysis.
articles.autores: Liu J, Wu Y, … Luo S (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Host defense against pathogen infection relies on coordinated immune activation and metabolic reprogramming, but how these processes are temporally organized in insects remains poorly understood. Here, time-series transcriptomic analyses of honey bee fat bodies revealed that Hafnia alvei infection induced a stage-dependent response. Genes involved in carbohydrate, glycerolipid, and glycerophospholipid metabolism were rapidly induced after infection, whereas immune signaling pathways and antimicrobial peptide genes were progressively upregulated later. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis further revealed positive correlations between lipid metabolism-related genes and immune genes, indicating tight coordination between metabolic and immune responses. Comparisons among germ-free, heat-killed bacteria-colonized, and conventionally colonized bees demonstrated that live gut microbiota promoted earlier and stronger lipid metabolic remodeling and immune activation, whereas heat-killed bacteria triggered delayed responses compared to live bacteria colonization. These findings indicate lipid metabolic reprogramming as a key component of honey bee defense against H. alvei and show that gut microbiota enhances host resistance by modulating metabolic-immune coordination.

articles.titulo: boosts host tolerance and mitigates virulence ofspecies in.
articles.autores: Mendiola SY, Safir WO, Vogel KJ (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Insects contend with myriad microbes throughout their lives. These microbial interactions, ranging from beneficial to pathogenic, have important consequences for the insect host, and simultaneous infection with multiple microbes is the norm. We are increasingly aware of how within-host interactions between the endogenous microbiota and invading pathogens can influence host infection outcomes. In this study, we examined how symbiont-pathogen interactions influence pathogen infection in the insect Rhodnius prolixus and how virulence can vary drastically with the context of infection, including cases where the endogenous microbiota is disrupted. Leveraging our ability to rear symbiont-free, or aposymbiotic, individuals, we first challenged symbiotic and aposymbiotic R. prolixus with three Serratia strains of varying virulence (two virulent Serratia marcescens strains and one avirulent Serratia ureilytica strain). We further altered the context of infection by varying the order of symbiont and pathogen colonization, as well as the method of inoculation (i.e., ingestion vs injection). Within R. prolixus, we showed a strong mitigating effect on virulence with the presence of Rhodococcus rhodnii, a well-established R. prolixus symbiont, despite high Serratia burdens. Virulence varied not only by Serratia strain but also by host species, with R. prolixus being particularly susceptible to infection among the four insect species tested. Our findings corroborate the importance of context in determining pathogen virulence, with symbiont presence, in particular, playing a key role in the outcome of pathogen infection for R. prolixus.IMPORTANCEThroughout their lives, insects encounter many bacteria, some beneficial and some detrimental. Increasingly, we are aware of how resident bacteria in the insect gut impact the ability of pathogenic microbes to establish and cause harm. Understanding the factors that underlie the specificity of these interactions is important in furthering our ability to leverage pathogenic microbes for the control of insect pests. This study focuses on the kissing bug, Rhodnius prolixus, a medically important insect that transmits Chagas disease. We tested the impact of different conditions in determining the virulence of the pathogen Serratia marcescens. Kissing bugs suffered high levels of mortality when infected with Serratia, particularly compared to other insect species. We determined that the presence of a beneficial bacterium (Rhodococcus rhodnii) in the kissing bug mitigated the ill effects of infection with Serratia. Early establishment of the beneficial bacteria was key to maximizing this effect.

articles.titulo: Magnitude and longevity of antibody responses to key Plasmodium vivax Erythrocyte Binding-Like proteins in an amazonian cohort: a long-term follow-up study.
articles.autores: Fernandes GM, Moreira-Nascimento SL, … Carvalho LH (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Plasmodium vivax, the second most common cause of malaria, remains a significant public health concern, with no vaccine approved to date. Although the DBL domain of Duffy binding protein (DBPII) is a leading blood-stage candidate, its extensive polymorphism, allele-specific immune responses, and low immunogenicity limit its effectiveness. In contrast, EBP2, a DBP homologue, emerges as a promising vaccine target due to its lower genetic variability and potential role in a distinct invasion pathway. Here, a long-term cohort of malaria-exposed individuals from the Amazon enabled the comparison of the magnitude and longevity of naturally acquired antibody responses to the DBL domains of EBP2 and DBP.
A 15-years follow-up study was carried out among long-term P. vivax exposed Amazonian individuals (363, median age 36 years) and included 10 cross-sectional surveys at periods of high and low malaria transmission. The experimental approach focused on the longitudinal monitoring of IgG antibodies against the full DBL domains of EBP2 and DBP, as assessed by conventional serology (ELISA). Antibody durability was estimated by time to the first documented loss of seropositivity (Kaplan-Meier), while repeated serological measurements over follow-up (GLMM) identified factors associated with seropositivity.
Regardless of the malaria transmission period, IgG reactivity and seroprevalence were consistently higher for EBP2 than DBPII. EBP2-dominant IgG antibody profile was detected in 68-88% of individuals, compared to 9-30% for DBPII. The median time of the first loss of DBPII seropositivity was estimated at 72 months, with EBP2 seropositivity remained above 50% throughout the 180-month follow-up period. Although time living in the study area was associated with antibody response to both antigens, malaria infection - predominantly submicroscopic - was identified as an independent predictor of anti-EBP2 IgG seropositivity.
EBP2 induces more robust and long-lasting IgG antibody responses than DBPII, even in the absence of frequent reinfection-induced boosting. Further studies are warranted to determine the protective role of naturally acquired anti-EBP2 antibodies in the Amazonian population.

articles.titulo: Recurrent features of stress response in the unicellular zygnematophyte Mesotaenium: intracellular inclusions and vacuoles forming upon UV.
articles.autores: Kunz CF, Ischebeck T, de Vries J (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The Zygnematophyceae, the closest algal relatives of land plants, many of which are unicellular, must manage environmental stress responses largely cell-autonomously, making them powerful models for dissecting the ancestral cellular toolkit underlying plant terrestrialisation. In this brief report, we revisit UV-B time-course experiment data on the unicellular zygnematophyte Mesotaenium endlicherianum, in which UV-B irradiation triggered a significant accumulation of terminal vacuoles. We re-analysed the corresponding RNA-seq data with a new focus on genes associated with vacuolar biology and lipid metabolism. Within 2 h of UV-B onset, homologs of genes linked to vacuolar functions in land plants were differentially expressed: transcripts of putatively lytic enzymes (a papain-like cysteine protease and two GH38 alpha-mannosidases), of a metal tolerance protein and of two AHK1-like histidine kinases increased, whereas those of the tonoplast H⁺-pyrophosphatase AVP1, the Ca²⁺/H⁺ antiporter CAX5 and the phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate 5-kinase FAB1A decreased. Lipid-related transcripts indicated a shift from membrane lipid biosynthesis towards lipid turnover, including the induction of a SUGAR-DEPENDENT 1-like triacylglycerol lipase. Based on homology, we propose the working hypothesis that UV-B shifts the vacuole from a homeostatic towards a stress-adapted state with altered ion homeostasis and increased lytic capacity. Together with reports of stress-associated vacuoles in other zygnematophytes, our data are consistent with an ancient role of the vacuole in streptophyte stress responses.

articles.titulo: Therapeutic potential of oncolytic Zika virus in NF1-associated tumors.
articles.autores: Ferreira RO, Ma HL, … Zatz M (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is an autosomal dominant disorder caused by pathogenic NF1 variants that drive aberrant Ras signaling and predispose individuals to tumors, including plexiform neurofibromas (PNFs) and malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs). These tumors remain challenging to treat: surgery is often unfeasible, MEK inhibitors provide only partial and temporary benefit, and no effective targeted therapies exist for MPNSTs. Here, we identify a previously unrecognized susceptibility of NF1-associated tumors to Zika virus (ZIKV). ZIKV efficiently infects Schwann cell-derived lines from PNFs and MPNSTs, activates viral replication, and triggers a robust pro-inflammatory cytokine response. Infection decreased viability by ∼60% in PNFs and ∼40% in MPNSTs and reduced Ki-67 expression, consistent with cytotoxic activity. Tumor spheroids exhibited pronounced structural disruption and increased cell death. Transcriptomic analysis linked ZIKV sensitivity to SOX10 and SOX2 expression in neural crest-like tumor cells. Most importantly, this finding was confirmed when fresh infected patient-derived samples were infected with ZIKV. These findings provide the first evidence that ZIKV can kill NF1-associated tumor cells and highlight its potential as a novel therapeutic strategy for PNFs and MPNSTs.

articles.titulo: Low Dissolved Oxygen Favors Biological Phosphorus Removal, and Oxygen Inhibition of PAOs Is an Important Part of the Story.
articles.autores: McIntosh L, Hiripitiyage D, … Bott C (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Conventional enhanced biological phosphorus removal (EBPR) design assumes dissolved oxygen (DO) concentrations between 2 and 4 mg/L are required to support reliable phosphorus removal, despite limited mechanistic evidence establishing the DO requirements of polyphosphate-accumulating organisms (PAOs). This study evaluated long-term EBPR performance, PAO oxygen kinetics, and predicted functional genes under high and low DO conditions. EBPR performance remained stable and improved at low DO, with median effluent orthophosphate concentrations at 0.2 mg DO/L 40% lower and less variable than at 2.0 mg DO/L. Batch testing revealed extremely low PAO oxygen half-saturation coefficients (KDO < 0.1 mg/L) and maximum phosphorus uptake rates at low DO, whereas elevated DO hindered phosphorus uptake. This inhibitory behavior was described using the Andrews model, indicating that high concentrations of DO can suppress PAO activity. Exploratory functional prediction from 16S rRNA gene data indicated differences in predicted stress-response and polyphosphate-related gene content between DO conditions, which identify candidate genes for future gene expression studies. These findings challenge conventional design guidance and motivate direct investigation of PAO oxygen inhibition.

articles.titulo: Variation in rhizosphere microbial communities and nitrogen- and phosphorus-cycling functional genes among rubber plantations in Yunnan, China.
articles.autores: Geng S, Yang J, … Yang C (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Rhizosphere microorganisms are important participants in soil nutrient transformation. However, variation in rhizosphere microbial community composition and nitrogen (N)- and phosphorus (P)-cycling functional gene profiles among rubber plantations in Yunnan Province remains unclear.
Metagenomic sequencing was used to compare rhizosphere microbial community composition and N- and P-cycling functional gene profiles among the rubber plantations located in five major natural rubber-producing areas in Yunnan Province, China: Gengma (MD), Ximeng (XM), Mengla (ML), Jinghong (JH), and Jiangcheng (JC).
Bacterial and fungal community composition and N- and P-cycling functional gene profiles differed significantly among the five rubber plantations. JC exhibited higher fungal diversity and richness, but its bacterial diversity was significantly lower than that in MD. The bacterial communities were dominated by Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota, and Actinomycetota, and the relative abundance of Acidobacteria was significantly enriched in JC compared to JH. Furthermore, Mucoromycota, Ascomycota, and Basidiomycota were the dominant phyla in the fungal community. At the functional level, compared to JC, key genes associated with N cycling were significantly enriched in ML, including N assimilation (glnA, gltB, gltD), dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (narG, narH, nirB), nitrification (nxrA, nxrB), and denitrification (napA, napB). Furthermore, the nosZ gene was also significantly enriched in MD compared to JC. Regarding the P cycle, compared to JC, genes associated with high-affinity phosphate transporters (pstA, pstB, pstC) and polyphosphate degradation (ndk) were significantly enriched in MD, whereas the organic phosphorus mineralization-related gene phnX exhibited the opposite trend. Meanwhile, compared to MD, the polyphosphate degradation-related gene ppk2 was significantly enriched in ML, whereas the inorganic phosphorus solubilization-related gene pqqC exhibited the opposite pattern. Hierarchical partitioning identified soil pH, total phosphorus (TP), and total potassium (TK) as the primary factors significantly associated with variations in bacterial community composition and P-cycling functional gene profiles.
In summary, the composition of rhizosphere bacterial and fungal communities, as well as the functional gene profiles related to N and P cycling, differed significantly among the investigated rubber plantations. These variations were closely associated with soil physicochemical factors. These findings may provide a microbiological basis for further developing site-specific nutrient management strategies in rubber plantations.

articles.titulo: Buyang Tongluo Decoction Mitigates Acute Ischemic Stroke by Suppressing NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD Pathway-Induced Pyroptotic Cell Death.
articles.autores: Lin H, Liu Y, … Wang K (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with neuroinflammation and pyroptotic cell death. The NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD signaling pathway plays an important role in ischemia-induced inflammatory injury. Buyang Tongluo Decoction (BTD), a modified traditional Chinese medicine formulation derived from Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BHD), may exert neuroprotective effects in AIS.
This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of BTD in AIS and their association with inhibition of pyroptosis pathways involving NLRP3, Caspase-1, and GSDMD.
A focal cerebral ischemia-reperfusion model was established using a modified filament occlusion technique. Experimental animals were assigned to four groups: sham controls, untreated model animals, BTD-treated animals, and a positive comparator group receiving BHD. Post-intervention evaluations included neurological assessment using Longa scores, cerebral perfusion analysis by laser speckle imaging, and quantification of ischemic lesions by 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining. Histological examination of brain tissue and neuronal architecture was performed using Nissl and hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining, and cellular ultrastructure was assessed using transmission electron microscopy. Protein expression levels of NLRP3, Caspase-1, GSDMD, and HIF-1α were analyzed by Western blotting, and inflammatory cytokine concentrations were determined by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The primary outcomes were neurological score and cerebral infarct volume. Secondary outcomes included cerebral blood flow, histological changes, ultrastructural findings, pyroptosis-related protein expression, and inflammatory cytokine levels.
Compared with the untreated model group, neurological impairment scores were significantly reduced in both the BTD and BHD groups, with BTD showing a greater trend toward neurological recovery. Cerebral perfusion was reduced and infarct volume was increased in untreated model animals, whereas these pathological changes were alleviated by BTD and BHD. BTD treatment was associated with marginally smaller infarct volumes than BHD. Histopathological examination of untreated specimens revealed substantial neuronal injury and disruption of tissue architecture, accompanied by characteristic pyroptotic changes at the ultrastructural level. Both interventions restored morphological and ultrastructural features. In addition, untreated model animals showed increased expression of pyroptosis-related proteins and elevated inflammatory markers, which were significantly suppressed after BTD and BHD administration. Comparative analysis indicated that BTD showed a stronger trend toward modulation of these molecular pathways.
Buyang Tongluo Decoction exerted neuroprotective effects by alleviating neurological dysfunction and reducing cerebral tissue injury. These effects were associated with the suppression of NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway-mediated pyroptosis and inflammatory responses.

articles.titulo: Three-dimensional organoid and organ-on-chip models for studying human viral infections: applications across respiratory, hepatotropic, enteric, cardiac, and neurotropic virus research.
articles.autores: Al-Attabi A, Mohammed MK, Hindi NKK (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Conventional two-dimensional cell lines and animal models each present well-recognized limitations for studying human viral infection: monolayer cultures lack tissue-level architecture and cellular heterogeneity, while species differences in receptor expression and immune physiology limit the translatability of animal data to human disease. Three-dimensional in vitro models, including air-liquid interface (ALI) transwell cultures, adult stem cell- and pluripotent stem cell-derived organoids, and microfluidic organ-on-chip platforms, have emerged as physiologically relevant alternatives that better recapitulate human tissue architecture, cellular diversity, and host-pathogen interactions. This review examines the application of these three-dimensional platforms across six domains of human viral pathogenesis: respiratory viruses (influenza, SARS-CoV-2, rhinovirus, respiratory syncytial virus) studied using ALI airway cultures, airway/lung/nasal organoids, and alveolar-capillary organ-on-chip systems; hepatotropic viruses (hepatitis B and C viruses) studied using perfused microfluidic liver cultures and patient-derived liver organoids capable of supporting complete viral replication cycles; enteric viruses (rotavirus, norovirus, coxsackievirus) studied using human intestinal enteroids and gut-on-chip systems; hemorrhagic-fever viruses (Ebola, Lassa) studied using microvessel-on-chip platforms; cardiotropic SARS-CoV-2 infection studied using engineered heart tissue; and neurotropic TORCH viruses (Toxoplasma, Other agents, Rubella, Cytomegalovirus, Herpes simplex virus - here represented by Zika virus and herpes simplex virus 1) studied using human brain organoids that recapitulate virus-induced microcephaly phenotypes. We compare the architecture, quantitative performance, strengths, and limitations of twenty-one representative platforms, position six platform classes on a physiological-relevance-versus-throughput landscape, summarize demonstrated applications in antiviral drug screening (including chip-based identification of amodiaquine and nafamostat repurposing candidates and a clinically important hydroxychloroquine false-positive), and extend the discussion to the translational challenges of donor variability, cross-laboratory standardization, throughput, and immune-cell integration that currently limit broader adoption of these models in preclinical virology and drug discovery pipelines.

articles.titulo: Integrated population genomics and phenotypic analyses reveal geographic structure and signatures of recent positive-selection underlying insecticide resistance in Anopheles arabiensis from The Gambia, West Africa.
articles.autores: Seck F, Mwangi JN, … Assogba BS (16 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Insecticide resistance in malaria vectors is spreading, with newly identified resistance markers raising operational challenges and threatening malaria reduction. Anopheles arabiensis is an important vector in The Gambia; however, the molecular basis of its insecticide resistance remains poorly understood. We observed signals of population structure between coastal and inland An. arabiensis populations in The Gambia, indicating restricted gene flow likely influenced by environmental variation. Pyrethroid and DDT resistance were widespread. However, the prevalence of both phenotypic and genetic insecticide resistance differed between coastal and inland populations. For instance, the Vgsc-L995S and Vgsc-L995F substitutions conferring pyrethroid and DDT resistance were more frequent in coastal populations and were associated with markedly higher phenotypic resistance to these insecticides. We also identified increased frequencies of copy number variation at Cytochrome P450 (Cyp6aa/p, Cyp9k1) and carboxylesterase (Coeae2-7 g) metabolic resistance markers in coastal An. arabiensis. Some observed gene amplifications were unique to Gambian coastal populations, suggesting their independent evolution. Furthermore, we found evidence of genomic regions under recent positive selection on chromosomes 2L:37,282,152-37,298,202 and 3R:28,590,243-28,602,280 with more pronounced selection signals observed among coastal populations. Coastal populations of An. arabiensis displayed an enrichment of resistance alleles, suggesting a localised pressure driving the evolution, selection and spread of resistance mechanisms. These findings underscore the importance of genomic surveillance in concert with bioassays to inform targeted vector control interventions. They also highlight the need to identify the sources and impacts of insecticide pressure acting on recently detected genomic regions under selection in the coastal regions of The Gambia.
