articles.titulo: Unlocking Nanocomposites via Cast Film Extrusion: Processing-Structure-Property Relationships of PLA Sheets Containing Silver Nanoparticles.
articles.autores: Lazaridou K, Ioannidis RO, … Bikiaris DN (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: A thorough investigation was conducted on poly(lactic acid) (PLA) nanocomposites based on silver (Ag) nanoparticles (NPs) as metallic nanofillers (from 0.5 to 5.0 wt%). The PLA Ag nanocomposite films were developed using the cast film extrusion technique. Gel permeation chromatography and intrinsic viscosity measurements revealed that cast film extrusion induced a significant reduction in the number average molecular weight of PLA, attributed to thermomechanical degradation, whereas the presence of NPs assisted and promoted the stability of the PLA films without further degradation. Proton nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed that the incorporation of Ag NPs did not induce any changes to the chemical structure of the polymer matrix. Scanning electron microscopy analysis showed an oriented morphology in neat PLA due to extrusion induced flow, whereas the addition of Ag NPs increased the surface heterogeneity. Differential scanning calorimetry results indicated that Ag NPs acted as nucleating agents, enhancing the degree of crystallinity of PLA. Complex segmental dynamics was revealed by dielectric spectroscopy, with the main segmental relaxation being accelerated and exhibiting an almost monotonic lowering of the cooperativity level with Ag NP loading. Partial densification of the polymer around the NPs and an increase in the free polymer volume away from them was expected. The mechanical performance was evaluated through tensile and flexural tests, where the presence of NPs enhanced the stiffness and strength of the samples, while the ductility was reduced. Annealing experiments also enhanced the mechanical performance of the materials. Finally, water contact angle measurements showed that the surface hydrophobicity was increased. Thus, in this study, PLA nanocomposites based on metal NPs produced via cast film extrusion were developed for advanced industrial applications; such nanocomposites are reported experimentally for the first time.

articles.titulo: Dynamic Determinants of the TLR4/MD2/Glycolipid Binding Unveiled Through Graph Neural Networks.
articles.autores: Martín-Cámara O, Arrayás-Ruiz Á, … Martín-Santamaría S (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide insights about the molecular world, but only if analyzed properly. Determining the relevant dynamics in a protein-ligand system often becomes the main bottleneck of the analysis. Here, we analyze the performance of graph neural networks (GNNs) trained on the MD simulations of several complexes of the innate immunity receptor TLR4/MD2 with different glycolipids to disentangle the atomic/molecular characteristics that determine the agonist/antagonist activity. By systematically evaluating distinct atomic subselections, we found that the classification performance of our model is higher for backbone-based subselections compared to all-atom representations. These findings indicate that dynamical differences in the agonist-antagonist behavior are primarily modulated by collective dynamics of TLR4/MD2 rather than specific ligand-residue interactions located at MD2. After analyzing the connectivity of the nodes along the simulations, MD2-polar rim and surrounding regions play a different behavior upon the binding of agonist or antagonist glycolipids, indicating a key role in the modulation of TLR4 activity. This work shows how MD simulation analysis through GNNs provides a powerful tool to extract meaningful atomic information to identify functionally relevant binding features in protein-ligand complexes.

articles.titulo: iMeta: Biology and medicine in informatics and MetaOmics era.
articles.autores: Li G, Yu Q, … Liu YX (169 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study presents a decade-long bibliometric map of informatics and metaomics research in biology and medicine, spanning life and agricultural sciences, basic and translational medicine, methodology innovation, and interdisciplinary frontiers. Aligning these findings with insights from the iMeta Conference 2026, which fostered talent cultivation and academic exchange among global researchers, we further highlight how the iMeta journal community captures the challenges and opportunities in this rapidly evolving era.

articles.titulo: Activity-Based Contracting for Insecticide-Treated Net (ITN) Mass Distribution Campaigns in the Democratic Republic of Congo: A Multi-province Quasi-experimental Evaluation.
articles.autores: Likwela JL, Luntadila MK, … Lukanu PN (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background Operational inefficiencies continue to limit the effectiveness of insecticide-treated net (ITN) mass distribution campaigns, particularly in challenging operating environments such as the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Results-based contracting has been proposed to improve campaign performance, but evidence regarding its effectiveness at scale remains limited. Materials and methods We conducted a quasi-experimental evaluation of ITN mass distribution campaigns implemented in 20 provinces of the DRC between 2022 and 2024, comparing four provinces applying an activity-based contracting (ABC) approach with 16 provinces applying the standard input-based approach. The primary outcome was compliance with ITN allocation norms, as verified by independent agencies. Secondary outcomes included independently verified household coverage, campaign preparation time, and unit cost per ITN distributed. Three comparison frameworks were combined: concurrent, within-province historical, and contextually matched. Because the ABC approach was assigned at the provincial level, we analyzed all indicators at both the household level (two-sample Z-tests for proportions with risk differences and 95% confidence intervals) and the provincial level (exact Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, with the province as the unit of observation). Results Compliance with ITN allocation norms was higher in ABC provinces than in non-ABC provinces (94.4% versus 85.6%; risk difference +8.8 percentage points, 95% CI +8.6 to +9.0). The difference persisted when province was the unit of analysis, with complete separation between the two groups: the four ABC provinces occupied the four highest ranks among the 20 (median 93.6% versus 85.6%; exact p = 0.0004). It was reproduced in the matched four-versus-four comparison (exact p = 0.029). All secondary outcomes were more favorable in ABC provinces: independently verified household coverage 98.6% versus 95.8%, adjusted campaign preparation time 14.6 versus 22.8 weeks, and unit cost USD 0.668 versus USD 0.773 per ITN distributed, but none reached statistical significance at the provincial level, and all are reported as exploratory. Measured ITN loss rates were higher under ABC (0.33% versus 0.17%); because losses were established by independent physical inventory under ABC and by administrative balance elsewhere, the two figures are not measurement-equivalent and were not compared statistically. Conclusions Scaling up ABC beyond a single pilot province was associated with higher compliance with ITN allocation norms, consistently across concurrent, historical, and matched comparison frameworks and at the level at which the intervention was assigned. Differences in coverage, timelines, and unit costs pointed in the same direction but were not statistically established. Results-based contracting merits consideration to improve the quality of large-scale distribution campaigns in resource-constrained settings, pending confirmation from evaluations conducted independently of program implementers and using designs that allow formal control of confounding.

articles.titulo: A neural circuit mediating altitude control in Drosophila.
articles.autores: Erickson AL, Omoto JJ, … Dickinson MH (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Flight is a remarkably efficient mode of locomotion that is largely responsible for the extraordinary evolutionary radiations of birds, bats, pterosaurs, and insects. Whereas walking animals need only control locomotion on a two-dimensional surface, flight requires active altitude regulation, a process by which the brain transforms self-motion cues into motor patterns that regulate lift. Using an integrative approach combining optogenetics, high-speed videography, two-photon imaging, robotics, and connectomics, we identified a single pair of descending neurons in Drosophila that control altitude. To search for candidate cells, we performed an optogenetic screen of sparse driver lines targeting descending neurons that project to the flight neuropil of the ventral nerve cord and identified one bilaterally paired neuron, DNa10, whose activation elicits changes in wing kinematics consistent with descent. A replay of the kinematics on a dynamically scaled robot confirmed that the wing motion elicited by DNa10 activation generates a reduction in upward force. Optogenetic activation of this neuron causes free-flying animals to descend, whereas ablation or silencing of the cell in tethered flies elicits fictive ascent. Functional imaging reveals that DNa10 is activated by downward visual motion and inhibited by upward motion. These results are consistent with a connectomic analysis showing that DNa10 receives monosynaptic input from large-field visual interneurons sensitive to vertical body motion and provides direct output to three wing motor neurons that regulate the lift. Collectively, these results identify core components of a circuit for altitude control that links the detection of visual motion to the alteration of aerodynamic forces.

articles.titulo: The β-ladder domain of TMUV NS1 enhances viral replication in avian cells by modulating its interaction with the NS4A-2K-NS4B complex.
articles.autores: Wang X, He Y, … Chen S (19 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Tembusu virus (TMUV), a mosquito‑borne flavivirus, represents a major threat to waterfowl farming in East and Southeast Asia. In vivo studies have noted distinct viral loads and viremia between ducklings infected with mosquito‑derived TMUV (mTMUV) and duck‑derived TMUV (dTMUV), yet the viral elements driving such phenotypic divergence remain unknown. The multifunctional nonstructural glycoprotein NS1 participates in flavivirus replication, secretion, and immune regulation. Here, we generated a panel of chimeric TMUV viruses with full‑length NS1 exchanges and NS1 domain substitutions based on mTMUV and dTMUV backbones. Our results demonstrated that NS1 modulates TMUV phenotypes in a strain-, dose-, and genetic background-dependent manner. Subcutaneous inoculation mimicking natural mosquito transmission amplified inter‑group phenotypic discrepancies, verifying NS1 as a pivotal modulator of TMUV‑triggered viremia. Since duck peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) infection underpins in vivo local viral establishment, an in vitro PBMC infection model validated the key contributory roles of NS1 and its functional domains in sustaining viral infection. We further utilized duck embryo fibroblasts (DEFs) to dissect the function of candidate NS1 domains. Domain swapping identified the β‑ladder domain as a major contributor to enhanced viral replication. Mechanistically, this replication enhancement effect correlates with strengthened interaction between NS1 and the NS4A-2K-NS4B replication complex. Collectively, our results identify the NS1 β-ladder domain as a critical determinant for TMUV infection. By modulating the interaction between NS1 and the NS4A-2K-NS4B complex, this domain regulates viral RNA replication efficiency in different hosts and consequently modulates viral dissemination and pathogenicity of TMUV.
Tembusu virus (TMUV) severely threatens waterfowl production across East and Southeast Asia. Noticeable phenotypic differences exist between mosquito-derived and duck-derived TMUV; however, the viral determinants responsible for this variation remain poorly understood. Although flavivirus NS1 is a multifunctional glycoprotein, how it mediates TMUV host-specific phenotypes remains incompletely characterized. Using chimeric and mutant viruses, this study demonstrates that the NS1 β-ladder domain enhances viral replication by strengthening the interaction with the NS4A-2K-NS4B replication complex. This domain governs TMUV replication efficiency across hosts, thereby controlling viral dissemination and pathogenicity. Our findings uncover a key molecular basis for TMUV host adaptation and provide insights into flavivirus mosquito-to-waterfowl transmission.

articles.titulo: Cross-Species and Cell-Type-Specific H3K27ac Dynamics Link Brain Aging to Alzheimer's Disease Genes.
articles.autores: Choo CT, Ngian ZK, Ong CT (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Active H3K27ac marks are dynamically remodelled during brain aging, but their cell-type-specific regulatory roles remain unclear. We integrated genome-wide H3K27ac profiles and transcriptomes from aging Drosophila heads, mouse NeuN+ forebrain neurons, and human NeuN+/NeuN- frontal cortex cells. In Drosophila, age-gained differential (Δ) H3K4me1 and H3K27ac peaks were associated with RNA processing and immune response genes, respectively, suggesting distinct regulatory programs. Despite limited biological replicates, mouse analyses revealed a strong association between promoter-associated ΔH3K27ac and synaptic gene expression in young neurons. Age-related gene-body H3K27ac loss coincided with increased expression of genes involved in GTPase signalling and vesicular transport. In humans (n = 29), NeuN- cells exhibited more age-associated ΔH3K27ac alterations than NeuN+ cells. Genes associated with age-gained peaks were enriched for gliogenesis and amyloid precursor protein metabolic processes, while age-related transcriptional changes associated positively with super-enhancer activity. Comparison with pan-tissue aging signatures revealed shared and cell-type-specific age-related ΔH3K27ac patterns in NeuN+ and NeuN- cells. Integrative analyses showed that age-gained ΔH3K27ac peaks in NeuN- cells overlapped with AD-associated ΔH3K27ac peaks, differentially expressed AD genes, and AD GWAS-linked variants, including those mapped to BIN1 and CR1. These findings highlight extensive H3K27ac remodelling in aging NeuN- cells and its convergence with AD-associated molecular alterations.

articles.titulo: Macrophage lipid metabolism: a hidden driver of aging and chronic diseases.
articles.autores: Li R, Tang X, … He M (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chronic metabolic diseases, such as type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and atherosclerosis, constitute a major burden on global health. The pathogenesis of these diseases is closely related to immune-metabolic disorders. Immunometabolism refers to the changes in intracellular metabolic pathways within immune cells that alter their functions. The lipid metabolism of macrophages is an important aspect of immunometabolism. Macrophages play a crucial role in tissue homeostasis and inflammatory responses through their plasticity. Aging macrophages show distinct lipid metabolic characteristics in comparison with young cells, which may be associated with the progression of chronic metabolic diseases. This article aims to explore how normal and aging macrophages affect the occurrence and development of chronic metabolic diseases.

articles.titulo: Systems medicine-driven drug repurposing for respiratory infections: insights into the oral-gut-lung microbial axis and the therapeutic potential of cannabidiol and aspirin.
articles.autores: L T, S S, P C (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The oral-gut-lung microbial axis plays a pivotal role in host immunity and respiratory disease pathogenesis; however, its systems-level integration with host-pathogen interactions remains poorly understood. This study presents a systems medicine framework to dissect the immunometabolic disruptions mediated by viral and bacterial respiratory pathogens and identify host-centered therapeutic targets through drug repurposing. A high-confidence host-pathogen interactome comprising 10,634 edges and 5605 nodes was constructed for nine clinically relevant pathogens, including Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTU), Bordetella pertussis, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Helicobacter pylori (HPY), Prevotella intermedia (PIT), Influenza virus, Herpes simplex virus, Human papillomavirus, and Epstein-Barr virus. Modular decomposition revealed three conserved hub modules (PIT, HPY, and MTU) and critical host regulators, such as ACTB, HSPA5, and ADORA1. Functional enrichment analysis indicated convergence in focal adhesion, immune checkpoint regulation, and metabolic stress responses. Drug repurposing via network centrality and Connectivity Map analyses identified cannabidiol and aspirin as potent multi-target agents capable of modulating key immune and signaling pathways. This study demonstrated the potential of integrative interactome analysis to inform host-directed, broad-spectrum therapeutic strategies and underscored the relevance of the oral-gut-lung microbial axis in shaping infection outcomes. This study provides a foundation for experimental validation and future precision medicine applications for respiratory infections.

articles.titulo: Adhesion G protein-coupled receptor A2 promotes tick-borne encephalitis virus replication by interacting with NS2B to enhance viral protease activity.
articles.autores: Tang J, Huang S, … Chen X (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) is a neurotropic flavivirus that causes severe neurological disease in humans, but the host factors required for its efficient replication remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify ADGRA2 as a novel host dependency factor for TBEV. Loss of ADGRA2, but not other ADGR family members, markedly restricts infection by multiple TBEV strains in human cells and primary mouse astrocytes. ADGRA2 is dispensable for viral entry but is required for efficient viral RNA replication, as demonstrated by impaired negative-strand RNA synthesis and accumulation of double-stranded RNA intermediates in ADGRA2-deficient cells. During infection, ADGRA2 is relocalized from the plasma membrane to the endoplasmic reticulum, where it functions independently of canonical WNT/β-catenin signaling. Mechanistically, ADGRA2 interacts with the viral cofactor NS2B, enhances NS2B-NS3 autocleavage and protease activity, promotes viral polyprotein processing, and facilitates NS2B/NS3 association with NS2A to enhance replication organelle biogenesis. ADGRA2 also promotes replication of Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV), Zika virus (ZIKV) and Dengue virus serotype 2 (DENV-2), suggesting a conserved role across flaviviruses. Together, these findings reveal that a host membrane receptor can be repurposed to drive NS2B-dependent protease maturation and replication complex assembly, thereby enabling efficient flaviviral replication.

articles.titulo: The role of MicroRNA profiles in antibody-dependent enhancement during dengue infection: impact on disease severity and therapeutic approaches.
articles.autores: Babai SF, Nourikhani M, … Nakhaie M (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue virus is a major mosquito-borne pathogen that causes clinical manifestations ranging from asymptomatic infection to severe dengue, including dengue hemorrhagic fever and dengue shock syndrome. Disease severity is strongly associated with antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE), in which pre-existing non-neutralizing antibodies promote Fcγ receptor-mediated viral entry into immune cells, resulting in enhanced viral replication, immune dysregulation, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular leakage. Emerging evidence indicates that microRNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators of host immune responses, inflammatory signaling, and vascular integrity during dengue virus infection. This review summarizes current evidence on the interplay between ADE and miRNA-mediated regulation of dengue pathogenesis, with emphasis on innate and adaptive immunity, Fcγ receptor signaling, cytokine responses, and endothelial barrier dysfunction. We also highlight circulating and tissue-specific miRNAs with potential value as biomarkers for disease severity and prognosis, and discuss emerging miRNA-based therapeutic strategies, including miRNA mimics and inhibitors, as host-directed approaches to modulate ADE-associated pathways. Improved understanding of miRNA regulatory networks may facilitate the development of novel biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies for severe dengue.

articles.titulo: Dietary Differentiation Among Sympatric Sri Lankan Bats Revealed by Nanopore Metabarcoding.
articles.autores: Perera T, Siriwardana S, … Kohl C (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Understanding trophic partitioning within multispecies bat assemblages is essential for evaluating their ecological roles in agroecosystems and disease-vector regulation. We assessed the diets of four sympatric cave-roosting bats in Sri Lanka-Hipposideros speoris, Miniopterus phillipsi, Rhinolophus rouxii, and Rousettus leschenaultii-using mitochondrial cytochrome b metabarcoding on the Oxford Nanopore platform. Across 22 fecal samples, we detected a diverse assemblage of Lepidoptera, Diptera, Coleoptera, and Hemiptera, including multiple agriculturally significant pest genera (e.g., Spodoptera, Cnaphalocrocis) and medically relevant vectors (Aedes, Anopheles, Phlebotomus). Preliminary data suggests Lepidoptera dominated the diets of M. phillipsi and R. rouxii, whereas H. speoris consumed proportionally more dipterans. Notably, insect DNA was detected in the frugivorous R. leschenaultii, may suggest facultative insectivory or incidental ingestion. Although statistical power was limited by uneven sample sizes and amount of samples, the results are suggestive of potential trophic differentiation among sympatric taxa. These findings provide baseline molecular dietary data for Sri Lankan bats and support their potential contribution to agroecosystem functioning and vector regulation within a One Health framework. However, this pilot study uses a snapshot sampling approach and can provide first insights and the baseline for further studies.

articles.titulo: Photoperiodic responses persist in DH-like neuropeptide gene mutants of the band-legged ground cricket, Dianemobius nigrofasciatus.
articles.autores: Shimizu Y, Kataoka K, Goto SG (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Seasonal adaptation is essential for the survival and reproduction of organisms inhabiting environments with predictable annual fluctuations. Photoperiodism is a key adaptive mechanism that enables most multivoltine insects to synchronize physiological and developmental processes with seasonal environmental changes, yet its underlying endocrine mechanisms remain poorly understood. Diapause hormone (DH) and DH-like neuropeptides, which belong to the tryptopyrokinin (TPK) family and are characterized by a conserved C-terminal WFGPRXa motif, play a pivotal role in photoperiodically regulated maternal embryonic diapause induction in several insect species. In some lepidopteran insects, DH has also been implicated in the regulation of photoperiodic responses beyond diapause induction, raising the possibility that DH/DH-like neuropeptides function as a common regulator of multiple photoperiodic responses across insects. However, whether this mechanism is conserved across insect taxa remains unclear. The band-legged ground cricket Dianemobius nigrofasciatus exhibits multiple photoperiodic responses, including maternal embryonic diapause induction, wing morph and rate of nymphal development. Here, we investigated the involvement of DH-like neuropeptides in photoperiodic responses in D. nigrofasciatus. Two genes encoding TPKs were identified from the genome sequence of D. nigrofasciatus. One corresponded to capa, whereas the other was designated Din-dh because it encoded seven TPKs (i.e., DH-like neuropeptides). We established three mutant lines carrying distinct Din-dh alleles derived from two G0 founders and investigated whether Din-dh is involved in photoperiodic responses. All mutant lines retained detectable photoperiodic responses. These results indicate that disruption of Din-dh does not abolish photoperiodic responses examined in D. nigrofasciatus.

articles.titulo: Effect of Graphene Oxide on the Microstructural Properties and Self-Healing Capacity of Well Cement Slurries Cured for Nine Years.
articles.autores: Jamrozik A, Malata G, … Jamrozik K (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The primary objective of well cementing is to achieve durable zonal isolation, thereby ensuring well integrity and safe long-term operation, which to a large extent depends on the proper design of the cement slurry formulation. In this context, particular importance is placed on the development of cement slurry formulations capable of withstanding harsh downhole conditions and producing set cement with modified microstructural properties and self-healing capacity. Graphene oxide (GO) is one of the potential nanoadditives that may support these mechanisms. Therefore, the aim of this study was to evaluate the long-term effect of GO on the microstructure and autogenous self-healing of microcracks in set well cement intended for wellbore sealing. Cement specimens prepared using CEM I 42.5 R Portland cement, with GO contents of 0.05% and 0.15% by weight of cement (bwoc), were examined after nine years of curing. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and micro-X-ray fluorescence (µ-XRF) analyses revealed microstructural features and elemental distribution patterns consistent with GO-induced modifications of the cement matrix. Observations of mineral precipitation within microcracks provided evidence of processes potentially contributing to autogenous crack sealing. Furthermore, porosity measurements demonstrated that the incorporation of GO into cement slurries with a water-to-cement ratio (w/c) of 0.7 reduces the pore volume, including the volume of capillary pores. These findings provide insights into the long-term microstructural behavior of GO-modified set cement and suggest its potential for developing advanced cement slurry formulations intended to enhance the durability of cement sheaths in hydrocarbon production, geothermal, and other demanding wellbore applications.

articles.titulo: Severe hyperchylomicronemia sensitizes the heart to pathological remodeling: evidence from GPIHBP1-deficient mice.
articles.autores: Fan R, Li J, … Liao J (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Circulating triglyceride and triglyceride-rich lipoprotein (TRL) accumulation is increasingly recognized as a residual atherosclerotic risk, but their specific effects on cardiac remodeling and heart failure (HF) remain largely unexplored. Here, this issue was investigated in Gpihbp1 knockout (KO) mice, which develop severe hyperchylomicronemia due to disruption of intravascular TRL hydrolysis.
Cardiac lipid metabolism and remodeling were evaluated in 10-month-old Gpihbp1 KO mice and their wild-type littermates under physiological conditions. Mice were also subjected to transverse aortic constriction (TAC) to evaluate the effects of severe hyperchylomicronemia on pressure overload-induced remodeling and HF. Furthermore, Gpihbp1 KO mice were crossed into an low-density lipoprotein receptor (Ldlr) KO background to study the effects of severe hyperchylomicronemia on hemorheology and high-fat diet (HFD)-induced cardiac pathology.
Untargeted cardiac lipidomics revealed 214 differentially regulated lipid species that were specifically enriched in glycerophospholipid, fatty acid (FA) and diacylglycerol subclasses. Quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) confirmed that FA oxidation-related genes were downregulated and that glucose utilization-related genes were upregulated. Electron microscopy revealed swollen mitochondria with fragmented cristae, and RNA-seq revealed reduced respiratory chain gene expression. These abnormalities resulted in impaired cardiac contractile performance in 10-month-old Gpihbp1 KO mice without the induction of hypertrophy or fibrosis. After TAC, Gpihbp1 KO hearts exhibited exaggerated diastolic dysfunction and more severe myocyte hypertrophy and fibrosis. In Gpihbp1/Ldlr double-knockout (dKO) mice, reduced erythrocyte deformability and increased whole blood viscosity were observed and worsened post-HFD. Additionally, HFD consumption resulted in significant diastolic impairment, cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis in dKO mice.
Severe hyperchylomicronemia due to Glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored high-density lipoprotein-binding protein 1 (GPIHBP1) deficiency sensitizes the heart to pathological remodeling and HF. These findings indicate a potential pathogenic contribution of hypertriglyceridemia and TRL accumulation to cardiac disease.

articles.titulo: Flame Retardancy and Hydrophobicity Enhancement for HDPE Containing an Organic-Inorganic Hybrid P-N-Si-Cu Cooperative Flame-Retardant System.
articles.autores: Li Y, Yan M, … Yang F (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: High-density polyethylene (HDPE) has been widely used as packaging and protection materials owing to its electrical insulation and mechanical strength. However, HDPE is flammable and requires flame-retardant modification. The addition of flame retardant leads to deteriorated compatibility of blends, reducing hydrophobic performance. Balancing the flame retardancy and hydrophobicity of the blend is challenging. Ammonium polyphosphate (APP) was modified by sequential loading of Cu-MOF followed by silane coupling agent treatment to prepare Si-Cu-APP, and lignin (Lig) was modified via piperazine-formaldehyde to obtain lignin-based organic skeleton (Pip-Lig). The Si-Cu-APP/Pip-Lig system achieves P-N-Si-Cu quaternary cooperative flame-retardant effect. while this system reduces the intramolecular hydroxyl content and weakens the polarity of the system. It makes the surface energy of the blend lower and improves its internal dispersion, forming an efficient hydrophobic protective layer. At a total additive loading of 30 wt%, the blend exhibits an LOI of 28.5%. The peak heat release rate (PHRR) decreases by 68.45%, and the total smoke production (TSP) decreases by 26.52%. Its water contact angle rises from 91.58° to 124.24°, water absorption decreases by 72%, and flame-retardant leaching is only 0.11%. This work provides an effective strategy for fabricating HDPE with simultaneously enhanced flame retardancy and hydrophobicity.

articles.titulo: Beyond Hematopoiesis: How Immune Are Hematopoietic Stem Cells?
articles.autores: Abnave P (1 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) have traditionally been viewed primarily as quiescent cells responsible for maintaining blood production, with their function defined largely by the progeny they generate. This view has changed considerably with growing evidence that HSCs actively sense and respond to inflammatory signals. HSCs express pattern-recognition receptors and diverse cytokine receptors, allowing them to detect infection and sterile inflammation directly or through signals from the bone-marrow niche. In response, HSCs can exit quiescence, alter their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, and support emergency hematopoiesis. Increasing evidence also suggests that inflammatory encounters can induce lasting epigenetic and metabolic changes in HSCs, shaping their subsequent responses and those of their progeny, a phenomenon associated with central trained immunity. HSCs can also express MHC class II and present antigen, suggesting functions beyond conventional stem-cell maintenance. However, immune responsiveness may also compromise HSC integrity. Acute, chronic, or repeated inflammatory exposure can induce replicative and metabolic stress, promote myeloid bias, alter clonal dynamics, and impair long-term self-renewal. Such changes may contribute to inflammaging and the development or expansion of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP). In this review, we synthesise evidence from experimental studies and recent literature to examine the emerging immune functions of HSCs and their consequences for stem-cell maintenance. We propose that HSCs should be viewed not as inert progenitors or conventional immune effector cells, but as immune-responsive stem cells that sense inflammatory challenges, adapt their behaviour, and influence the output and function of the innate immune system. TEASER ABSTRACT: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) are increasingly recognised as active responders to inflammation rather than passive precursors of immune cells. They sense inflammatory signals, adapt proliferation and lineage output, and retain epigenetic and metabolic memory that can shape subsequent haematopoiesis. However, chronic inflammation can impose replicative stress, impair self-renewal, and promote clonal selection and ageing. This review proposes that HSCs are best viewed as immune-responsive stem cells linking inflammatory sensing and adaptive haematopoiesis to both trained immunity and long-term stem-cell vulnerability.

articles.titulo: Injectable Nanozyme-Polyphenol GelMA Hydrogel for Mitochondrial Immunomodulation and Periodontal Bone Protection: An in vitro and in vivo Study.
articles.autores: Lin J, Zhou Y, … Huang X (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Periodontitis involves persistent oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysregulated macrophage activation. This study aimed to develop and evaluate an injectable nanozyme-polyphenol GelMA hydrogel (TCM-Gel) for local periodontal therapy.
TCM-Gel was characterized for physicochemical, antioxidant, and catalase-like properties. Its effects on macrophage mitochondrial indices, inflammatory phenotype, and human gingival fibroblast responses were evaluated in vitro using three independent biological replicates. A ligature-induced mouse periodontitis model included healthy control, Ligature + PBS, and Ligature + TCM-Gel groups (n = 5 mice per group), and local tissue response was assessed in 3 mice.
TCM-Gel formed a porous, mechanically resilient hydrogel with pH-dependent component availability, radical-scavenging activity, and catalase-like H2O2 decomposition. In LPS-challenged macrophages, TCM-Gel increased the CD206/CD80 ratio (~1.85, P < 0.001), increased the JC-1 red/green ratio (~6.7) compared with the control (~3.2) and GSH (~4.2) groups, reduced intracellular ROS (~8% vs ~95% in the H2O2 positive control, P < 0.001), and increased CAT activity (~5.1 vs ~2.3 in the control group, P < 0.001). SIRT1, SDHB, UQCRC2, and ATP5A transcript levels increased by approximately 5.2-, 2.7-, 2.9-, and 7.2-fold, respectively (all P < 0.001). In hGFs, TCM-Gel attenuated ferroptosis-associated marker changes, including reduced p53 and ACSL4 and increased GPX4 levels (all P < 0.001), and improved mineralization and osteogenic marker expression. In vivo, TCM-Gel reduced inflammatory infiltration, osteoclast activity, and alveolar bone loss, and increased CD206, endomucin, and SIRT1 immunoreactivity. Micro-computed tomography showed that BV/TV increased from 19.10 ± 2.47% in the Ligature + PBS group to 25.42 ± 0.44% in the TCM-Gel group.
TCM-Gel was associated with improved redox status, macrophage mitochondrial indices, pro-resolving macrophage-marker expression, and periodontal bone preservation. These findings support further evaluation of this nanozyme-polyphenol hydrogel as a local periodontal nanomedicine platform.

articles.titulo: The Immune Paradox in Acute Anorexia Nervosa: A Hypothesis Linking Hyperactivity, Restrained Inflammation, Preserved Innate Defense, and Constrained Adaptive Immunity.
articles.autores: Smith LL (1 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a severe psycho-metabolic disorder characterized by persistent energy restriction and substantial loss of adipose tissue. Despite profound undernutrition and measurable immune alterations, individuals with acute AN (AN-acute) have been reported to experience fewer clinically evident infections than expected from conventional models of malnutrition. This creates an apparent immune paradox. Scope of Review: Immune findings in AN are heterogeneous, reflecting differences in illness duration, eating-disorder subtype, nutritional severity, and methodology. Furthermore, persistent physical activity, a prominent feature of AN-acute, has received relatively little attention despite its important immunomodulatory effects in healthy individuals. This review presents a hypothesis integrating concepts from exercise physiology and immunometabolism with findings on immune function in AN-acute. Hypothesis: The immune phenotype of AN-acute may reflect selective allocation of limited energy, consistent with immunometabolic principles. It is proposed that severe energy restriction may permit sufficient neutrophil- and macrophage-mediated innate defense to contain pathogens early while constraining the more metabolically demanding activation and expansion of adaptive immunity. At the same time, multiple metabolic and endocrine mechanisms may restrain systemic inflammation, potentially reinforced by repeated contraction-derived IL-6 myokine signaling associated with persistent hyperactivity. Conclusions: This model proposes that preserved innate containment, constrained adaptive escalation, and restrained systemic inflammation interact in AN-acute to reduce the clinical expression of infection. It offers a testable framework linking starvation, hyperactivity, immunometabolism, and immune function.

articles.titulo: Obesity-Induced Alterations in Linezolid Tissue Distribution Revealed by Dynamic Positron Emission Tomography Imaging.
articles.autores: García-Varela L, Gómez-Martínez M, … Mondelo-García C (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The rising prevalence of obesity and its associated susceptibility to infection raise concerns about the adequacy of fixed linezolid dosing. Obesity-related alterations in tissue drug exposure remain poorly characterised. This study quantified the in vivo biodistribution and pharmacokinetics of linezolid in diet-induced obese and control mice using positron emission tomography (PET).
Male C57BL/6J mice received a high-fat (n=6) or standard diet (n=8) for ten weeks. [¹⁸F]F-Linezolid was produced by copper-mediated ¹⁸F-fluorination of a boronic ester precursor under optimised low-base conditions. Following intravenous administration, dynamic whole-body PET images were acquired over 90 minutes, followed by computed tomography (CT) imaging. Volumes of interest (brown and subcutaneous white adipose tissue, heart, knee, brain, and lung) were analysed using radioactivity concentration, total radioactivity, standardised uptake values, and kinetic modelling with an image-derived input function. Plasma radiometabolites were quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography.
[¹⁸F]F-Linezolid was obtained with >99% radiochemical purity and molar activity of 28-92 GBq/µmol. Obese mice showed lower blood radioactivity, with comparable parent-fraction profiles between groups. The one-tissue compartment model and Logan analysis provided optimal fits. Volume of distribution was significantly reduced in obese animals exclusively in adipose depots, accompanied by lower influx rate constants, whereas exposure was fully preserved in lung, brain, and bone/joint tissue.
Obesity induces selective pharmacokinetic alterations confined to adipose compartments without compromising linezolid delivery to clinically relevant target tissues, revealing a plasma-tissue dissociation and a tissue-specific distribution that may limit the interpretation of plasma-based therapeutic drug monitoring.

articles.titulo: Mitochondrial Fatty Acid Oxidation Dysregulation in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: Mechanistic Roles and Emerging Diagnostic and Therapeutic Advances.
articles.autores: Wang SY, Shang DF, … Zhao WX (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is a chronic metabolic liver disorder driven by the convergent effects of obesity, insulin resistance, lipid overload, gut-liver axis disruption, and immune inflammation. Mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation is central to the disposal of excess fatty acids and the maintenance of hepatocellular energy homeostasis; under sustained metabolic stress, however, this process can shift from an adaptive response to a molecular hub for incomplete oxidation, oxidative injury, inflammatory amplification, and fibrotic progression. This review examines fatty acid uptake and activation, carnitine-dependent transport, sequential β-oxidation, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, electron transfer, mitochondrial quality control, and immunometabolic crosstalk, and explains how diet, circadian disruption, aging, gut dysbiosis, drug exposure, and genetic susceptibility destabilize oxidative homeostasis through defined molecular pathways. From a translational perspective, we propose a functional-endotype framework that integrates imaging, acylcarnitine profiling, lipidomics, oxidative-damage markers, inflammatory and fibrotic indices, and genetic risk to guide stratified interventions targeting thyroid hormone signaling, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors, incretin pathways, bile-acid signaling, fibroblast growth factors, energy-sensing networks, and precision nanomedicine.

articles.titulo: G-CN-Orchestrated Multi-Component Synergy for Enhanced Flame Retardancy in PLA.
articles.autores: Kuo YT, Marquez JAD, … Wang Q (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Polylactic acid (PLA) is a biodegradable polymer with good processability, but its poor flame retardancy limits its wider practical use. In this work, an ethanol-assisted pre-assembled g-C3N4/fumed silica hybrid (gCNFS) was introduced into a PLA/ammonium polyphosphate (APP)/lignin system to improve its flame-retardant performance. The pre-assembly strategy was designed to improve the interfacial contact between g-C3N4 and fumed silica and regulate char formation and thermal decomposition during burning. The chemical structure and morphology of the composites were analyzed to study their thermal degradation behavior, volatile release, and post-burn char morphology. The results showed that the introduction of pre-assembled gCNFS improved the flame retardancy of the PLA/APP/lignin system. Among all formulations, PLA/Q-gCNFS-3 exhibited the best overall performance, achieving a limiting oxygen index (LOI) of 37% and a UL-94 V-0 rating. Compared with neat PLA, its peak heat release rate (pHRR) and total heat release (THR) decreased by approximately 50% and 24%, respectively, indicating effective suppression of burning intensity and total heat output. The flame-retardant mechanism of PLA/APP/Lignin with gCNFS enhanced both condensed-phase and gas-phase flame-retardant actions. In the condensed phase, a continuous and compact expanded char layer with better sealing ability and barrier performance was formed. In the gas phase, nonflammable gas release occurred, which helped reduce the concentration of combustible volatiles. Hence, the ethanol-assisted pre-assembled gCNFS is an effective strategy for improving the flame-retardant efficiency of PLA/APP/lignin composites.

articles.titulo: Ion regulatory mechanisms supporting hypersaline tolerance in the coastal rock pool mosquito.
articles.autores: Chiang J, Khodikian E, … Matthews BJ (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The coastal rock pool mosquito, Aedes togoi, is a remarkable example of a saline-tolerant mosquito. While most mosquitoes are obligate freshwater breeders, Ae. togoi larvae and pupae inhabit coastal rock pools that span freshwater to hypersaline conditions. We explore the ability of Ae. togoi larvae to tolerate hypersaline conditions by profiling the salt gland, an ion regulatory nexus within an anatomically unique, elaborated anal canal. We present a de-novo chromosome-scale genome assembly for Ae. togoi, highlighting its relatively small genome size and differences in chromosomal structure as compared to other Aedine mosquitoes. We detail repeat content and curate key multi-gene families encoding ion-transport proteins enriched in the larval salt gland, building a model of the machinery that likely facilitates hyperosmotic urine formation. Our work provides insights into molecular and anatomical adaptations that underpin the ability of mosquitoes and other insects to thrive in hypersaline rock pools and other dynamic environments.
