articles.titulo: Development of a sustained-release 1-Octen-3-ol nanoparticle formulation via molecular docking-guided design and response surface optimization for enhanced mosquito attraction.
articles.autores: Wang C, Li X, … Chen J (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Mosquito-borne diseases pose a major global health burden, and effective attractants are essential for vector surveillance and control. 1-Octen-3-ol (octenol) is a known mosquito attractant but suffers from high volatility and short effective duration. In this study, molecular docking confirmed its strong binding to mosquito olfactory receptors, providing theoretical support for its attractant activity. To address this limitation, the aim was to develop a nanoparticle encapsulation strategy for sustained release and enhanced stability.
Molecular docking confirmed strong binding affinity between octenol and mosquito olfactory receptors, supporting its attractant activity. Formulation and process parameters were screened via single-factor experiments and optimized using response surface methodology. Under the optimized conditions, octenol-loaded nanoparticles (octenol NPs) exhibited a mean particle size of 142.5 nm, a polydispersity index of 0.1383, a zeta potential of -16.2 mV, a drug loading of 10.9%, and an encapsulation efficiency of 70.2%. Physicochemical characterization demonstrated the favorable stability of octenol NPs, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed successful drug encapsulation. In outdoor mosquito-attraction assays, octenol NPs were 2.98-fold higher than that of an equivalent amount of free octenol in attracting mosquitoes and significantly prolonged the effective half-life of attraction.
Nanoparticle encapsulation overcomes octenol's volatility and short activity duration. The optimized octenol NPs provide an efficient, long-lasting mosquito-attractant formulation for vector control. Furthermore, this work establishes a flexible nanocarrier platform for the sustained release of volatile semiochemicals, bridging attractant research with practical applications in mosquito control, and offering broader potential for agricultural arthropod pest management. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.titulo: The yeast inositol polyphosphate kinase Kcs1 is a signaling node phosphorylated by the mitogen-activated protein kinase Kss1.
articles.autores: Decker SJ, Landry GA, … Kumar A (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The Kss1 mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade is a conserved signaling module regulating the yeast stress-responsive transition from planktonic single cells to a filamentous pseudohyphal growth state. The Kss1 signaling network is expansive and incompletely defined, encompassing orthologs of oncogenes and fungal virulence determinants. Notably, KSS1 is required for wild-type inositol polyphosphate (InsP) signaling. InsPs are soluble and highly charged second-messengers generated by the action of kinases on the six-carbon cyclitol inositol. Kcs1 is an InsP kinase that generates pyrophosphorylated InsP7, and we previously identified Kcs1 as a phosphorylation substrate of the AMPK ortholog and pseudohyphal growth regulator Snf1. Here, we investigated Kcs1 regulation by Kss1, as overexpression of KCS1 suppressed defective pseudohyphal growth in the kss1 deletion mutant. Purified Kss1 phosphorylates a MBP-Kcs1 fragment in vitro at serine residues 115 and 183. Mutation of these sites to alanine decreased in vivo InsP7 levels relative to wild type, and the kcs1-S183A mutant exhibited defective pseudohyphal growth. A phosphomimetic mutant substituting Glu (E) for Kcs1 S183 underwent pseudohyphal growth at levels comparable to wild type. The Kcs1 sites phosphorylated in vitro by Snf1 and Kss1 are separate, and serine-to-alanine mutations of fourteen sites encompassing those targeted by Snf1 and Kss1 (in kcs1-S14A) resulted in decreased InsP7 levels and diminished pseudohyphal growth. The kcs1-S183A and kcs1-S14A mutants displayed fragmented vacuolar morphologies with hypersensitivity to tunicamycin. Collectively, the data identify Kcs1 as a node for AMPK and MAPK signaling, highlighting the importance of InsPs in nutrient stress responses and vacuolar biology.

articles.titulo: Factors associated with malaria parasitemia in hospitalized children under five years of age with severe acute malnutrition in Burundi: a retrospective cross-sectional study.
articles.autores: Rajaguru V, Fiston NB, … Han W (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria and severe acute malnutrition (SAM) are among the leading causes of morbidity and mortality in children under 5 years of age in sub-Saharan Africa. When these conditions occur, they interact synergistically, exacerbating disease severity and compromising child survival.
This study aimed to determine the prevalence of malaria parasitemia and identify factors associated with malaria parasitemia among children under five years of age with severe acute malnutrition admitted to Butezi District Hospital, Burundi, between 2023 and 2024.
A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted using the medical records of children under 5 years of age diagnosed with SAM at Butezi District Hospital, Burundi. Malaria parasitemia was diagnosed using either microscopy or rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs), according to routine hospital practice. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the study population. Associations between SAM and malaria parasitemia were examined via chi-square tests and logistic regression models. Statistical significance was established at p < 0.05.
A total of 481 children under five years of age with SAM were included in the study. Malaria parasitemia was detected in 150 (31.2%) children. Among all participants, 275 (57.2%) were diagnosed using microscopy and 206 (42.8%) using RDTs. Girls had higher odds of malaria parasitemia than boys (OR = 1.52, p = 0.042), while children who did not use mosquito nets had nearly twice the odds of malaria parasitemia (OR = 1.97, p = 0.002). Compared with children whose fathers were farmers, those whose fathers were civil servants (OR = 0.18, p < 0.001) or merchants (OR = 0.21, p < 0.001) had significantly lower odds of malaria parasitemia. In sex-stratified analyses, edema (aOR = 2.00, p = 0.037) and lack of mosquito net use were significantly associated with malaria parasitemia among boys, whereas age younger than 6 months (aOR = 3.21, p = 0.034) was significantly associated with malaria parasitemia among girls.
Integrated interventions addressing both malnutrition and malaria, alongside targeted prevention strategies, are essential to reduce child morbidity and mortality in resource-limited settings.

articles.titulo: Effects of bile acids and gut microbiota interactions on neurological and psychiatric disorders.
articles.autores: Pei X, Wang X, … Xu H (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The gut-brain axis, as a bidirectional communication network connecting the gut microbiota to the central nervous system, plays a key role in a variety of neurological and psychiatric disease processes. In recent years, researchers have discovered that bile acids (BAs) are important signaling molecules that extend beyond their traditional role in lipid digestion and absorption. They are now known to play a significant role in regulating metabolism, immunity, and nervous system functions. Notably, gut microbes dynamically regulate BA profile through deconjugation, dehydroxylation, and other biotransformations, building a complex regulatory network of microbial-host co-metabolism, which in turn modulates gut-brain axis function through multiple receptors. Specifically, BAs precisely regulate neuroimmune homeostasis, dynamic balance of the blood-brain barrier, and neurotransmitter metabolism through the activation of membrane and nuclear receptors, such as farnesoid X receptor (FXR), takeda G protein-coupled receptor 5 (TGR5), pregnane X receptor (PXR), vitamin D receptor (VDR), and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 2 (S1PR2), a mechanism that provides a new perspective for elucidating the pathogenesis of neurological and psychiatric diseases. In this review, we systematically elucidate the microbial regulatory mechanisms of BA metabolism, focusing on the pathways through which BA-gut microbiota interactions affect neurological and psychiatric disorders via the neuroimmune pathway. By integrating the latest research evidence, we systematically sort out the key signaling pathways mediated by BA receptors and their neuroimmune regulatory networks, and provide a theoretical framework for the development of targeted intervention strategies for psychiatric disorders based on the regulation of the gut-brain axis.

articles.titulo: Biomarkers of Immune Injury in Cardiometabolic Disorders.
articles.autores: Zhou L, Li Y (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cardiometabolic disorders are accompanied by persistent immune activation that links metabolic stress to vascular and organ injury. Conventional inflammatory measures capture part of this process, but they provide limited information about tissue origin, biological mechanism and disease trajectory. This narrative review examines emerging biomarkers across genetic and epigenetic regulation, metabolic and oxidative stress, gut microbial exposure, innate immune activation, adaptive immune remodeling and circulating inflammatory responses. It integrates mechanistic studies with clinical observations to consider how these signals may inform the assessment of cardiometabolic immune injury. Particular attention is given to the distinction between inherited susceptibility and acquired responses, circulating associations and tissue mechanisms, and potentially injurious versus compensatory immune activity. The evidence supports substantial biological connectivity among these domains, while the strength of clinical validation varies widely. Most candidate markers and proposed combinations require standardized measurement, longitudinal assessment and external validation before biomarker-guided prevention can be justified. We propose a mechanism-informed framework for organizing candidate immune-metabolic phenotypes, recognizing reciprocal interactions rather than a universal temporal sequence. Future studies should determine whether these biomarkers improve prediction and clinical decisions beyond established risk factors and whether changes in biomarker profiles correspond to meaningful treatment benefits.

articles.titulo: Application of Biological Invasion Models in Epidemiology: Analysing the Spatial Distribution of Dengue Fever Cases Based on the Suitable Habitats of Aedes Mosquitoes.
articles.autores: Li C, Lan F, … Liu J (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study explores the application of biological invasion models in epidemiology by examining the spatial relationship between dengue fever transmission and the suitable habitats of Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus in China. By integrating invasion biology and epidemiological modelling perspectives, the study applies the MaxEnt model to predict mosquito suitable habitats using occurrence records and environmental variables, and further combines the spatial Durbin model to analyses the direct and indirect spatial effects of mosquito distribution on dengue incidence. Results reveal significant spatial correlations between mosquito habitats and dengue outbreak regions. A. aegypti exhibits stronger direct effects on local dengue transmission, suggesting higher infectivity within suitable habitats, whereas A. albopictus demonstrates stronger spatial spillover effects, indicating greater diffusion capacity across regions. The findings highlight the value of integrating species distribution modelling with spatial econometric analysis to improve understanding of vector-borne disease diffusion and support targeted prevention and control strategies from an interdisciplinary systems perspective.

articles.titulo: Systematic Investigation into Biochar-Mediated Suppression of Asphalt Rubber Fumes: Inhibition Mechanism, Pollutant Profiles, and Binder Performance.
articles.autores: Yao Z, Zhang B, … Li S (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Asphalt rubber (AR) is increasingly used as a sustainable pavement binder, but hazardous fumes generated during production constrain its wider application. This study investigated wood biochar (WB), walnut-shell biochar (WSB) and corn-straw biochar (CSB) as sustainable fume-suppressing additives for AR binders. The biochars were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), elemental analysis (EA), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and N2 physisorption tests, while AR emissions were evaluated through real-time monitoring of total volatile organic compounds (TVOC), H2S, SO2 and NOX, together with thermal desorption-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (TD-GC-MS) analysis. Conventional binder properties and rheological behavior were also evaluated. The results showed that WSB possessed the most developed hierarchical pore structure, with a Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of 285.8 m2/g and a total pore volume of 0.165 cm3/g, achieving the strongest TVOC reduction (65.6%) and the lowest detectable organic-fume complexity. TD-GC-MS analysis showed that WSB mainly reduced the relative responses of aliphatic hydrocarbons and PAH-related hydrocarbons, whereas WB selectively reduced BTEX/alkylbenzenes and S/N-containing responses. CSB, enriched in ash-derived minerals and oxygen-containing groups, exhibited the strongest sulfur-gas suppression, achieving complete SO2 elimination and 57.65% H2S inhibition, but also induced a redistribution toward oxygenated organics and alicyclic hydrocarbons. Biochar addition generally improved high-temperature stiffness and compatibility. These findings demonstrate feedstock-dependent and pollutant-specific suppression behavior, suggesting that physical adsorption and surface chemical interactions may jointly contribute to fume suppression, and provide guidance for selecting biochar additives for cleaner AR production.

articles.titulo: Shared and subtype-specific lipidomic signatures precede ischemic stroke and intracerebral hemorrhage.
articles.autores: Lu L, Chen Q, … Jiang Y (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Altered redox homeostasis is increasingly recognized as an important contributor to cerebrovascular injury in stroke, yet relevant prospective population-based evidence on pre-diagnostic lipid remodeling remains limited. We aimed to characterize shared and subtype-divergent lipidomic signatures preceding ischemic stroke (IS) and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Within a nested case-control design in the Taizhou Longitudinal Study, 1103 incident IS cases, 159 incident ICH cases, and 1277 matched controls underwent high-coverage lipidomic profiling (1067 species across 37 subclasses). We identified a shared lipid signature across IS and ICH characterized by elevated acylcarnitines and sphingosine-1-phosphates and reduced phosphatidylserines and phosphatidylethanolamine plasmalogens. We further found that lipid structural features, including higher unsaturation and longer acyl-chain length in some lipid subclasses, were associated with increased stroke risk, whereas higher plasmalogen proportion was inversely associated. In contrast, neutral lipids showed subtype-specific patterns. Triacylglycerols (TAGs) and free fatty acids (FFAs) were broadly associated with IS risk, whereas predominantly very-long-chain species were linked to ICH. Network analysis supported divergent remodeling, showing altered TAG-FFA-acylcarnitine correlations in IS and reduced plasmalogen connectivity in ICH. Moreover, we developed subtype-specific lipid scores that showed promising discriminatory performance in internal validation. For IS, the AUCs were 0.63 (0.59-0.68) for the clinical model, 0.88 (0.85-0.90) for the lipid model, and 0.89 (0.86-0.91) for the combined model. The corresponding AUCs for ICH were 0.65 (0.55-0.75), 0.82 (0.75-0.87), and 0.86 (0.79-0.91), respectively. In an independent temporal validation, the AUCs were 0.60 (0.56-0.64), 0.76 (0.72-0.79), and 0.77 (0.73-0.80) for the clinical, lipid, and combined model of IS, and 0.62 (0.51-0.73), 0.72 (0.63-0.80), and 0.81 (0.75-0.87) for those of ICH, respectively. In conclusion, these findings identify shared and subtype-divergent lipidomic signatures preceding IS and ICH, with potential relevance to redox homeostasis.

articles.titulo: Cu-Cu Grain Intermixing Quantification for Hybrid Bonding Applications.
articles.autores: Kumar A, Velmurugan J, … Buckalew B (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cu-Cu hybrid bonding at reduced thermal budgets depends critically on reliable grain intermixing across the bonding interface. Yet interfacial evolution is still predominantly assessed qualitatively, precluding objective comparison across copper microstructures and process conditions. Here, we introduce Bond IQ, an automated image-based metrology framework that converts registered cross-sectional FIB-SEM datasets into physically interpretable descriptors using classical computer-vision methods. We apply the framework to five blanket chip-level pairings spanning three engineered copper microstructures: coarse-grain (CG), fine-grain locked (FG-L), and fine-grain thermally dynamic (FG-TD) Cu, thermocompression bonded at 210 °C for 2 h. Three coupled but distinct metrics are extracted: Bridged Interface Fraction (BIF), Interface Void Loading (IVL), and normalized Grain Penetration Depth (GPD). The symmetric CG/CG interface exhibited the weakest evolution, combining high IVL (5.4 nm) with low BIF (6.1%) and low GPD (0.20). By contrast, CG/FG-TD achieved the highest BIF (54.5%) at low IVL (0.6 nm), signifying broad but comparatively shallow bridging, whereas CG/FG-L reached the highest GPD (0.89) at moderate BIF (32.7%), indicating localized yet deeper directional grain advancement. Among symmetric fine-grained interfaces, FG-L/FG-L displayed the lowest IVL (0.5 nm), underscoring the role of fine-grain stability in void suppression. Collectively, these results demonstrate that interface bridging, void elimination, and penetration depth are governed by distinct but interrelated contributions of grain-size contrast and microstructural stability. By reducing subjective interfacial assessment to quantitative, mechanistically interpretable descriptors, Bond IQ offers a scalable route to screen copper microstructures and bonding conditions, and it can be extended to other metal-metal interfaces where microstructural evolution governs low-temperature bonding reliability.

articles.titulo: Ligand-Specific Remodeling of theRDL GABA Receptor by the A296S Mutation Differentiates Recognition of Fipronil and Fluralaner.
articles.autores: Al-Akeel RK, Ibrahim IM, … Ezat AA (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-gated chloride channel Resistance to Dieldrin (RDL) receptor is a major molecular target of insecticides, yet the structural basis by which resistance-associated mutations differentially influence chemically distinct ligands remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the effects of the classical A296S substitution on the interactions of the Anopheles gambiae RDL receptor with the phenylpyrazole fipronil and the isoxazoline fluralaner using homology modeling, molecular docking, 200 ns molecular dynamics simulations (apo receptors and three independent replicas of each ligand-bound complex), and MM/PBSA free-energy calculations that include an interaction-entropy (IE) term. Apo-state molecular dynamics simulations showed that A296S preserved the overall structural stability of the receptor while locally modifying the environment of the pore-lining M2 transmembrane helix. Although docking scored fluralaner more favorably than fipronil in both receptor variants, the replicated molecular dynamics simulations revealed ligand- and genotype-dependent behavior. In the wild-type receptor, fluralaner remained stably bound and had a favorable MM/PBSA free-energy estimate (-18.3 ± 4.2 kcal/mol), whereas the ligand RMSD of fipronil increased progressively and its estimate was close to zero (+1.2 ± 9.5 kcal/mol). In the A296S model, the fipronil estimate was similar (+1.6 ± 4.3 kcal/mol), but the fluralaner estimate became unfavorable (+10.0 ± 1.8 kcal/mol), and Ser296 itself contributed slightly unfavorably to both ligands. Together, these findings indicate that A296S does not act as a universal determinant of ligand recognition but is associated with ligand-specific changes in the modeled interaction landscape, with the larger predicted effect on fluralaner. These predictions derive from a homology model, were not tested by electrophysiology or binding assays, and do not measure functional resistance. They may nonetheless help inform the interpretation of cross-resistance patterns and structure-guided efforts targeting GABA receptor-based insecticides.

articles.titulo: Exercise-nutrition-myokine-mitochondrial interactions in immune aging: an immunometabolic framework for host defense.
articles.autores: Peng R, Pan Y, … Jiang Y (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Exercise is increasingly recognized as a systemic modulator of immune and metabolic physiology, with potential relevance to immune aging, chronic low-grade inflammation, and host defense. This structured narrative review integrates evidence on the interplay among exercise, skeletal-muscle-derived signaling, mitochondrial adaptation, and nutritional context to develop a conceptual framework for immunometabolic reprogramming during immune aging. Literature was identified through searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar using combinations of terms related to exercise, myokines/exerkines, mitochondria, nutrition, immunosenescence, inflammaging, and host defense. We synthesize evidence across human, animal, and cellular studies, while distinguishing direct human findings from associative and preclinical mechanistic evidence. Particular attention is given to exercise-induced myokine signaling, mitochondrial biogenesis and function, metabolic flexibility, redox signaling, and mitochondrial quality control, as well as the potential modifying effects of macronutrients, amino acids, fatty acids, micronutrients, and dietary bioactive compounds. The review further considers how exercise and nutritional context may influence features of immunosenescence and inflammaging and examines their potential relevance to vaccine responses and infection-related host defense. Importantly, changes in circulating biomarkers or immune-cell phenotypes are not assumed to represent improved immune competence or clinical protection. Instead, the available evidence is interpreted according to exercise modality and dose, training status, age, sex, nutritional and metabolic context, and the level of biological evidence. Overall, this framework highlights the potential for exercise-nutrition interactions to shape immune-metabolic communication while emphasizing that several proposed myokine-mitochondrial-immune links remain associative or mechanistic hypotheses requiring prospective human investigation.

articles.titulo: Impact of infliximab combined with methotrexate on serum inflammatory and immunometabolic biomarkers in rheumatoid arthritis.
articles.autores: Al-Maslamani B, Soudi S, Al-Ghazaly ZM (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory disease associated with metabolic reprogramming of immune cells. Although inflammatory cytokines have been extensively studied, the effects of disease-modifying therapies including methotrexate, infliximab and their combination on serum immunometabolic biomarkers remain incompletely understood.
This cross-sectional study included newly diagnosed RA patients, patients receiving MTX monotherapy, patients receiving MTX plus infliximab, and healthy controls. Serum levels of tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-10 (IL-10), lactate, citrate, and succinate dehydrogenase (SDH) activity were measured. Disease activity was evaluated using the Disease Activity Score in 28 joints (DAS28). Statistical analyses, hierarchical clustering, correlation and network analyses, principal component analysis (PCA), and exploratory structural equation modeling (SEM) were used to investigate immunometabolic relationships and treatment-associated changes.
Newly diagnosed RA patients showed significantly elevated TNF-α, IL-10, lactate, SDH activity, TNF-α/IL-10 ratio, and DAS28, alongside reduced citrate levels compared with controls and treated patients. Combined MTX and infliximab therapy demonstrated the greatest improvement in inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers and the lowest disease activity. Multivariate analyses identified TNF-α, lactate, and DAS28 as major contributors to disease-associated variation, while citrate displayed an opposing metabolic pattern. Correlation and network analyses identified TNF-α as a central link between inflammation, metabolic remodeling, and disease severity. SEM suggested that treatment-associated reductions in TNF-α were related to decreased glycolytic activity, improved mitochondrial metabolism, and reduced disease activity.
RA involves coordinated inflammatory and metabolic dysregulation. Combined MTX and infliximab therapy appears more effective than MTX alone in restoring immunometabolic balance.

articles.titulo: The Immunological Biography of the Carotid Plaque: From Trained Immunity and Clonal Lymphocytes to Spatial Immune Niches and Plaque Vulnerability.
articles.autores: Krasiński Z, Raffa GM, … Urbanowicz T (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Atherosclerotic carotid plaques are shaped by years of interaction between systemic risk factors, hematopoietic conditioning, vascular injury, and local immune responses, yet conventional assessment captures only a limited snapshot of this biological history. This review introduces the concept of the "immunological biography" of the carotid plaque and examines how trained innate immunity, macrophage state and defective resolution, adaptive immune memory, T- and B-cell clonal selection, and spatially organized immune niches contribute to plaque heterogeneity and vulnerability. The literature was identified through a structured PubMed search complemented by reference screening, with emphasis on human carotid tissue, paired blood-plaque studies, immune-repertoire analyses, and single-cell and spatial technologies. Current evidence indicates that immune-cell abundance alone incompletely characterizes plaque biology: functional state, antigen experience, clonality, tissue localization, and interactions with vascular and stromal cells provide additional levels of biological information. We propose the Carotid Plaque Immune Phenotype (CPIP) as an integrative framework linking systemic immune history with cellular state, clonal architecture, spatial organization, and clinically relevant plaque features. Combining circulating biomarkers with tissue-resolved immune profiling may ultimately improve biological phenotyping of carotid atherosclerosis and provide a framework for prospective studies linking plaque immune architecture with cerebrovascular events.

articles.titulo: Role of the Tregs-Endothelial Cell Interaction Network in Immune Microenvironment Remodeling and Targeted Intervention in Cardiovascular Diseases.
articles.autores: Mo L, Gao J, … Bai Y (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The pathogenesis of cardiovascular disease (CVD) involves immune and metabolic remodeling of the vascular microenvironment, in which interactions between regulatory T cells (Tregs) and endothelial cells are important. Tregs can support endothelial homeostasis through immunoregulatory cytokines, whereas endothelial signals may influence Treg activity. This network has context-dependent effects in CVD: Tregs suppress inflammation, preserve endothelial barrier integrity, and promote repair, whereas Treg dysfunction, metabolic dysregulation, or age-related changes can impair endothelial function and accelerate disease progression. This review examines how glycolysis-lactate signaling, hypoxic metabolic adaptation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and redox imbalance shape Treg-endothelial crosstalk and immune microenvironment remodeling in CVD. We also discuss molecularly targeted interventions, cell-based and engineering approaches, and metabolic therapies directed at this network. Finally, we consider how spatial and single-cell multi-omics can identify disease-associated Treg and endothelial states, map their interactions, and link transcriptional programs to metabolic dysfunction. This metabolic perspective may guide mechanistic studies and the development of targeted therapies for CVD.

articles.titulo: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics for studying cell competition in the tumor microenvironment.
articles.autores: Balu P, Sureshkumar A, … Wong LS (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cell competition is a conserved fitness-surveillance process, first described in Drosophila epithelia, by which cells compare relative fitness with their neighbors so that less-fit "loser" cells are eliminated, extruded or forced to differentiate while fitter "winner" cells expand. In the tumor microenvironment (TME), this logic appears to be co-opted by transformed clones that eliminate normal epithelium, outcompete neighboring subclones and reshape stromal and immune compartments, making cell competition a potentially underappreciated contributor to cancer clonal evolution, immune escape and therapy resistance. Because competition is defined by a comparison between adjacent cells and by a demonstrated change in the relative representation of one population, it is difficult to resolve with bulk sequencing, which averages across precisely the heterogeneity that defines it. The convergence of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, spatial and single-cell proteomics, artificial intelligence (AI) and network-inference bioinformatics now allows competition-relevant cellular states, interfaces and signaling relationships to be measured at the resolution the problem requires. We emphasize at the outset that these technologies are, in almost all current applications, hypothesis-generating: they identify candidate competitive interfaces and putative winner and loser states from static measurements, and they do not by themselves demonstrate that competition has occurred. This review synthesizes advances across these domains; proposes an explicit three-tier evidence framework separating direct experimental evidence of cell competition from competition-relevant associations and from computational predictions; distinguishes cell competition from related processes such as clonal selection, immune editing and differential proliferation; and defines a putative cell competition network as a falsifiable construct whose edges include ligand-receptor, spatial-adjacency, metabolic and mechanical relations. We further outline a conceptual, context-dependent Cell Competition Score (CCS) as a testable specification rather than a biomarker-ready instrument, and set out the benchmarking, causal-inference and prospective-validation requirements that stand between current capability and any clinical application.

articles.titulo: Pore-Size-Dependent Competitive CH/COAdsorption in HRTEM-Informed Short-Chain-Aromatic Organic-Matter Nanopores of Coal-Measure Shale.
articles.autores: Long M, Li K, … Wu J (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study investigates pore-size-dependent competitive CH4/CO2 adsorption in coal-measure shale organic-matter nanopores represented by HRTEM-informed short-chain aromatic fragments. Coal-measure shale from the eastern Yushe Block of the Qinshui Basin was selected as the research object. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy was employed to quantitatively characterize the aromatic lamellar structure of the organic matter. Based on the obtained structural parameters, organic-matter pore models with pore sizes ranging from 1 to 4 nm were constructed. Grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations were subsequently performed to investigate the single-component and competitive adsorption behaviors of CH4 and CO2 at temperatures of 288-308 K and pressures of 0.25-8 MPa. The results indicate that the aromatic structure of the organic matter is characterized by short chains and a low degree of condensation, while the pore system is dominated by micropores and small mesopores. CH4 exhibited its highest nominal-pore-volume-normalized adsorption in the 1 nm pore, consistent with micropore filling, whereas CO2 reached its maximum in the nominal 2-3 nm pore models. These maxima may be influenced by model geometry and normalization because the probe-accessible pore volumes and surface areas after annealing were not quantified. In the smaller 1 and 2 nm pore models, CO2 exhibits a pronounced competitive adsorption advantage. As the pore size increases to 3-4 nm, the relative adsorption capacity of CH4 increases, thereby narrowing the adsorption difference between CH4 and CO2. These findings provide molecular-scale insights into pore-size-dependent equilibrium CH4/CO2 adsorption in experimentally informed organic-matter nanopores, offering a reference for future evaluations of CO2-enhanced gas recovery and storage in coal-measure shale.

articles.titulo: Molecular basis of reproductive plasticity in termites under environmental stresses and prediction of colony fecundity using machine learning.
articles.autores: Ye CX, Zhang WX, … Su XH (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The reproductive plasticity of social insects provides colonies with tremendous flexibility to respond to environmental changes and adapt to new habitats. However, understanding how gene networks regulate this plasticity to generate complex social phenotypes remains a challenge. Here, we propose an "inhibition-activation-reinhibition" model for the reproductive transformation of female workers using three species of Reticulitermes termites. Through transcriptomic analysis of female workers during this dynamic cycle, we identified functional genes involved in their reproductive transformation. We found that gene expression profiles in female workers responded strongly to queen loss. Furthermore, we confirmed that under severe environmental stress that threatened colony survival, the workers did not activate the gene regulatory networks associated with reproductive transformation. We also demonstrated that piggyBac and tigger transposable element-derived genes in the workers' brains cooperatively promoted reproductive transformation. Metabolomic changes in female workers were linked to stress signals from queens and the nest environment, primarily involving fatty acid and amino acid metabolism pathways. Finally, we constructed seven machine learning models to elucidate gene expression profiles related to reproductive plasticity and to predict the presence and loss of female reproductives (queens, which are indicators of colony fecundity). Among these, the deep neural network models showed the highest accuracy and practicability for analyzing gene regulatory networks and predicting caste. We propose that female workers, as indicators, carry extensive colony-specific information at the transcriptomic level. These findings provide valuable insights and innovative methodologies for understanding reproductive plasticity in social insects under environmental stress.

articles.titulo: Tirzepatide and inflammation: a critical reappraisal of the immunometabolic case for incretin-based therapy.
articles.autores: Jabbar AD (1 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, lowers high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) by 29-55% across randomised trials in obesity, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obstructive sleep apnoea, and interleukin-6 by 25-30% at 72 weeks. Much of this is not weight-mediated: in SURPASS-4 the fall in hsCRP correlated with that in body mass index at r = 0.07, and mediation analysis of trials of semaglutide, a selective GLP-1 receptor agonist, attributes only 21-62% of its hsCRP effect to change in glycated haemoglobin and/or weight. The mechanism, however, is not the one usually given: the account reproduced in most reviews, that incretin receptors on macrophages and T lymphocytes signal through cyclic AMP to restrain nuclear factor-κB, is not supported by the best-controlled data. The principal antibody used to detect the T-cell GLP-1 receptor gives signal in receptor-null cells; Glp1r is undetectable by quantitative PCR in peritoneal and adipose macrophages; and haematopoietic receptor deletion does not abolish semaglutide's anti-atherosclerotic effect. I therefore propose a three-route model, graded by evidence: limited direct signalling in a few validated lymphocyte populations, a central neuro-immune relay, and a large indirect metabolic contribution. That adipose macrophages are refractory to tirzepatide while Kupffer cells respond, and that C-reactive protein is hepatocyte-derived, suggest a substantially hepatic rather than adipose effect. Because the mechanistic evidence concerns GLP-1 receptor agonism almost entirely, the appraisal applies to incretin-based therapy as a class, tirzepatide being the worked example. Five falsifiable propositions are advanced with the experiments that would refute them.

articles.titulo: Chromosomal confirmation of the separate species status of(Geoffroy in Fourcroy, 1785) and(Paykull, 1800) (Coleoptera, Elateridae).
articles.autores: Angus RB, Maury A (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Karyotypes, with C-banding, are given for Melanotus villosus (Geoffroy in Fourcroy) and M. castanipes (Paykull). The preparations are from mid-gut and gonads of adults, and mid-gut and testis of larvae. M. villosus has 2n = 18 + X (♂), 18 + XX (♀), while M. castanipes has 2n = 20 + X (♂), 20 + XX (♀). The X chromosome of M. villosus is the smallest in the nucleus, while in M. castanipes it is among the largest. Heterochromatin is confined to small centromeric C-bands in both species. The differences between the karyotypes of the two species in both total number chromosomes present and in particular the size of their X chromosomes are sufficient to confirm that two distinct species are involved.

articles.titulo: Altered ER-mitochondria contact sites in neurons: Mechanisms and functional implications.
articles.autores: Tsuboi M, Shibayama K, Hirabayashi Y (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are distributed throughout all neuronal compartments, where they control diverse biochemical processes. Recent studies have shown that these organelles do not function independently but instead form specialized physical interfaces known as mitochondria-ER contact sites (MERCS), which enable coordinated biochemical regulation. Although MERCS were first identified in neurons more than 50 years ago, and alterations in MERCS have been implicated in various neurological disorders, their physiological roles and regulatory mechanisms have only recently begun to emerge. In this review, we highlight recent advances in understanding neuronal MERCS, focusing on insights gained from volume electron microscopy (volume EM or vEM), genetically encoded imaging tools, and genetic manipulation of mitochondria-ER tethering proteins. Elucidating the spatiotemporal regulation and physiological functions of MERCS will provide insight into how subcellular compartmentalization expands the functional complexity of neurons, thereby supporting the brain's remarkable information-processing capacity within a limited volume.

articles.titulo: Evidence of co-circulation and co-exposure to arboviruses and malaria in a longitudinal cohort in Kenya from 2019 to 2022.
articles.autores: Tariq A, Bisanzio D, … LaBeaud AD (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), dengue virus (DENV), and malaria have gained significant concern in sub-Saharan Africa. The similar epidemiology, endemicity and clinical presentation of the diseases caused by these pathogens underscore the need to investigate the burden and emergence of mixed infections and the potential factors that increase the risk of coexistence and co-circulation of these pathogens. In this study, we determine the burden of co-exposure and co-infection of CHIKV, DENV, and malaria in Kenya and describe the associated risk factors. We followed 4,534 study participants from December 2019 to February 2022 on the coast (Ukunda) and west (Kisumu) of Kenya to quantify the burden of CHIKV, DENV, and malaria co-infections and recent and lifetime co-exposure. The results highlight 15.5% acute malarial infection, 0.7% acute DENV infection, and 0.06% acute CHIKV infection in our cohort. No acute co-infection was detected. The lifetime co-exposure to DENV and malaria was 0.75% and CHIKV and malaria was 1.8%. We estimated ~ 0.2% of the study population to be co-exposed to DENV, CHIKV, and malaria. The study highlights the importance of higher socioeconomic status, mosquito prevention methods, and sleeping under the bed nets to decrease the co-exposure to DENV, CHIKV, and malaria and, crowding and presence of water containers to increase the co-exposure to DENV, CHIKV, and malaria.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-65333-7.

articles.titulo: Home sweet home-a breath full of fresh air or a lungful of woes: A cross-sectional study to explore determinants of indoor air pollution and factors influencing the use of unclean fuels.
articles.autores: Nagdoune N, Mahajan R, Giya H (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Household air pollution from solid fuel use remains a major public health concern in India, particularly among women and young children. Community-level data that capture coexisting indoor combustion exposures, housing characteristics, and program uptake barriers are limited.
This study aimed to describe the prevalence and pattern of indoor air pollution exposures, housing characteristics, self-reported respiratory symptoms, and Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) awareness and uptake in an urban slum community.
A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted in 3 urban slums within the field practice area of a tertiary care institution in western India. Sample size (n = 139) was calculated using National Family Health Survey-5 estimates (10% unclean fuel use). Systematic random sampling was used. One adult respondent, either the woman responsible for cooking or the household decision-maker, was interviewed. Descriptive statistics were calculated, followed by chi-square tests for bivariate associations and logistic regression for exploratory multivariable analysis.
Biomass fuel use was reported in 47.1% households. Multiple concurrent exposures were common: indoor smoking, mosquito coil use, and frequent incense burning. Poor housing conditions included inadequate ventilation, absence of a separate kitchen, and lack of exhaust systems. Although 80.4% were aware of the PMUY, only 16.7% had utilized it. In multivariable logistic regression, no household-level variable was significantly associated with unclean fuel use; PMUY awareness showed borderline association with uptake, and confidence intervals were wide across models, reflecting limited statistical precision.
Multiple modifiable indoor pollution sources coexist within poorly ventilated households, suggestive of a need for integrated interventions targeting cleaner fuels, improved ventilation, and effective program implementation.

articles.titulo: Immunosenescence remodels the osteoimmune microenvironment in osteoarthritis: from cellular crosstalk to regenerative therapeutics.
articles.autores: Liu R, Zhu Z, … Huang C (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Osteoarthritis (OA) has evolved from a condition conventionally regarded as mere mechanical "wear and tear" to a complex, whole-joint disorder driven by chronic low-grade inflammation and cellular dysfunction. Within the joint, the osteoimmune microenvironment-composed of articular cartilage, synovium, subchondral bone, the infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP), and resident stem cell niches-serves as the central site of osteoimmune interaction for maintaining tissue homeostasis and repair. Accumulating evidence indicates that age-associated dysregulation and senescence of innate and adaptive immune cell subsets represent major contributors to OA progression. Age- and senescence-associated immune states generate persistent inflammatory, oxidative, and damage-associated signals that contribute to microenvironmental deterioration. In this review, we propose a unified framework elucidating how immunosenescence reshapes the osteoimmune microenvironment via aberrant intercellular communication. We systematically delineate the distinct cellular crosstalk networks connecting immunosenescent drivers with chondrocytes, synovial fibroblasts, subchondral bone remodeling units, IPFP adipocytes, and mesenchymal stem/stromal cells (MSCs). Furthermore, we highlight emerging therapeutic avenues to reprogram this senescent niche, encompassing senotherapeutics, immunometabolic reprogramming, biomaterial-assisted targeted delivery, and engineered cell therapies. Finally, we propose the "Resolution Failure Hypothesis" as a testable mechanistic framework in which impaired efferocytosis and dysregulated specialized pro-resolving mediator (SPM) signaling may contribute to the persistence of osteoimmune remodeling. Rather than proposing defective inflammation resolution as a new biological phenomenon, this framework integrates established resolution-related mechanisms with age-associated immune remodeling and asks whether insufficient restoration of clearance and resolution capacity helps explain the incomplete structural recovery observed after senescent-cell-targeted interventions. Reconceptualizing OA through the lens of immunosenescent crosstalk will accelerate the translation of disease-modifying therapies from microenvironmental modulation toward functional joint regeneration.

articles.titulo: Neuropeptide T2A-GAL4 Knock-Ins Illustrate Practical Considerations for Interpreting GAL4 Reporter Patterns in Drosophila.
articles.autores: Jinnai K, Ozawa K, … Kondo S (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Transgenic GAL4 lines are widely used in Drosophila to label and manipulate specific cell types, but the resulting reporter expression patterns do not always represent ongoing driver activity. We generated a collection of neuropeptide T2A-GAL4 knock-ins and developed fluorescent Brp knock-ins that serve as neuropil markers, enabling native-fluorescence imaging without immunostaining. The reporter patterns of these GAL4 drivers were broadly consistent with previously reported expression of the corresponding neuropeptides. During characterization, we observed both timing-dependent changes in adult GFP labeling and GAL4-associated cellular abnormalities. Using temperature-sensitive GAL80, we found that adult GFP labeling in certain neurons driven by CCHa2-T2A-GAL4 and Dsk-T2A-GAL4 depended on GAL4 activity before eclosion and was not reproduced by adult-restricted induction. Several GAL4 lines also showed dominant developmental phenotypes. Heterozygous Burs-T2A-GAL4 animals, for example, displayed wing expansion defects that were fully suppressed by GAL80. Severe wing defects were not accompanied by a reduction in the number of reporter-labeled neurons before eclosion, but the morphology of these neurons was affected. These observations illustrate how developmental driver history and GAL4-associated cellular effects can influence reporter patterns in the adult nervous system.

articles.titulo: Fire Performance, Thermal Degradation and Combustion Products of Flame-Retardant Hybrid Epoxy Composites.
articles.autores: Mizera K, Sałasińska K (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The fire performance of hybrid epoxy composites depends on both the flame-retardant system and the reinforcement architecture. This study investigates the effects of different combinations of synthetic and natural fabrics and functional fillers on the fire behavior, thermal degradation, smoke production, and combustion products of epoxy composites containing 10 wt.% expandable graphite (EG) and 10 wt.% ammonium polyphosphate (APP). A glass-fiber-reinforced composite was used as the reference. The materials were characterized by cone calorimetry, smoke density measurements, horizontal burning tests, thermogravimetric analysis (TG/DTG), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), simultaneous thermal analysis coupled with Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (STA/FT-IR), and combustion-effluent analysis using a Purser furnace coupled with a Gasmet DX4000 gas analyzer. Significant differences in fire performance were observed among the formulations. VACMGBHF exhibited the longest time to ignition (206 s), the lowest peak heat release rate (79 kW·m-2), and the lowest maximum mass-loss rate during the principal thermo-oxidative degradation stage (2.03%·min-1). It also retained 38.8% of its initial mass at 900 °C, the highest value among the hybrid composites. In contrast, ACGBF showed the lowest average heat release rate (8 kW·m-2), maximum average rate of heat emission (20 kW·m-2), and total heat release (4 MJ·m-2). Smoke production also depended on composite composition. The lowest maximum specific optical density was recorded for the glass-fabric reference (42), whereas ACGBF exhibited the lowest total smoke release (123 m2·m-2). Visual examination revealed differences in the continuity and morphology of the post-combustion residues, with several hybrid formulations forming expanded, cohesive carbonaceous-mineral layers. TG/DTG, DSC, and STA/FT-IR analyses further demonstrated formulation-dependent degradation behavior and evolved-gas profiles. All composites achieved the HB classification in the horizontal burning test. The findings demonstrate that reinforcement architecture and filler composition influence heat release, smoke generation, and thermal stability in different ways, highlighting the need to evaluate these parameters together when designing flame-retardant epoxy composites.

articles.titulo: A Phosphorus-Containing Polyamide Oligomer as a Synergist for Flame-Retardant PA66/GF Composites: Concurrent Improvements in Flame Retardancy and Electrical Safety.
articles.autores: Zhang X, Xie L, … Huang D (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: As electronics become smaller and more power-dense, glass-fiber-reinforced polyamide 66 (PA66/GF) must combine halogen-free flame retardancy with electrical safety, including a glow-wire ignition temperature (GWIT) ≥ 775 °C and a comparative tracking index (CTI) ≥ 600 V. Conventional low-molecular-weight flame retardants often require loadings above 15 parts by mass, impairing mechanical and electrical properties. Here, a phosphorus-containing polyamide oligomer (DOPO-MA-oligomerPA6) was synthesized via a DOPO-MAH intermediate from 9,10-dihydro-9-oxa-10-phosphaphenanthrene-10-oxide (DOPO) and maleic anhydride (MAH), followed by polymerization with ε-caprolactam, then melt-blended with aluminum diethylphosphinate (ADP) and melamine polyphosphate (MPP) in PA66/GF. Its oligo-PA6 backbone provides good compatibility with PA66, while its low molecular weight (Mn = 10,984 g mol-1; PDI = 2.569) favors dispersion. The phosphorus groups enhance the efficiency of the ADP/MPP system. With 4 parts oligomer and a total flame-retardant loading of 14 parts by mass per 100 parts PA66/GF, the composite achieved UL-94 V-0 rating, a limiting oxygen index (LOI) of 36.1%, a GWIT of 800 °C, and a CTI of 600 V. Its heat deflection temperature, tensile strength, notched impact strength, and flexural modulus were 178.8 °C, 95.0 MPa, 8.7 kJ m-2, and 8984 MPa, respectively. Compared with the conventional 20-part system, total additive loading decreased by 30%, with simultaneous improvements in flame retardancy, electrical safety, and mechanical properties. This offers a scalable route to high-performance PA66/GF composites.

articles.titulo: A century of mosquito diversity and distribution in Haiti and the Dominican Republic (1905-2024).
articles.autores: St-Louis D, Boussès P, … Roiz D (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquito-borne diseases represent a major public health threat, particularly on islands and in resource-limited settings. Hispaniola, the second-largest island in the Caribbean, shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic, is highly vulnerable to such diseases due to recurrent extreme climatic events, endemic diseases such as malaria, filariasis and dengue, and challenging socio-economic and political conditions that hinder effective vector control. Moreover, knowledge of mosquito (Diptera: Culicidae) biodiversity and distribution on the island is outdated and fragmented. We conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of mosquito species diversity and associated vector-borne diseases in both countries, covering the period 1905-2024, using the Web of Science and PubMed databases, as well as grey literature and entomological collections. The data were synthesised into an updated checklist and historical distribution maps. A total of 1604 occurrence observations were extracted from 82 studies, of which 1369 unique occurrence observations were retained after deduplication. Our review identified 13 genera and 62 mosquito species on the island, of which 12 species are exclusive to the Dominican Republic, one is exclusive to Haiti and 49 species are shared by both countries. There was greater species richness in the Dominican Republic, with 61 species, compared with Haiti, with 50 species, likely reflecting differences in topography, land use and research efforts. The most frequently reported species were Aedes aegypti, Anopheles albimanus, Ae. albopictus, Culex quinquefasciatus, Cx. nigripalpus and Psorophora jamaicensis. This updated checklist and distribution analysis covers the last 120 years and is the first harmonised, comprehensive long-term synthesis of culicid biodiversity in Haiti and the Dominican Republic to date. It provides a critical foundation for risk assessment and the design of integrated vector management and surveillance strategies to address future mosquito-borne disease threats in the region.

articles.titulo: Dengue emergence risk in Tehran, Iran: An integrative review ofecology, climate, urban environmental determinants, and public health preparedness.
articles.autores: Abbasi E, Talbalaghi A (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
To synthesize the available evidence concerning Aedes mosquito ecology and potential establishment, climatic and environmental suitability, epidemiological and urban determinants, and public health surveillance and preparedness relevant to dengue emergence in Tehran, Iran. The review also aimed to distinguish environmental receptivity and potential vector establishment from documented autochthonous dengue transmission and to identify key evidence gaps and surveillance priorities.
Structured narrative/integrative review.
A structured literature search was conducted covering publications and relevant publicly available information from January 2000 to March 2025. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and selected Iranian institutional sources were searched.
Aedes vector ecology and potential establishment; climatic and environmental suitability; epidemiological, population-level, urban, and infrastructural determinants; and vector surveillance, control, and public health preparedness. Twelve core studies were selected for focused qualitative and integrative analytical synthesis. Evidence was interpreted according to its geographical relevance and methodological basis, distinguishing direct Tehran-specific findings from Iranian, regional, international, and model-based evidence.
Available evidence did not demonstrate sustained establishment of Aedes aegypti or Aedes albopictus populations or sustained autochthonous dengue transmission in Tehran. However, climatic variability, warming trends, urban environmental conditions, potential breeding habitats, population mobility, and regional entomological evidence indicate potentially relevant conditions for future environmental receptivity. Climate and spatial models suggest possible expansion of environmental suitability for Aedes vectors and dengue-related transmission under warming scenarios, although these projections do not establish local vector populations or demonstrate dengue transmission in Tehran. Important limitations in standardized longitudinal entomological surveillance and integrated epidemiological and laboratory monitoring remain.
Tehran is best characterized as a setting of potential and evolving dengue receptivity rather than established dengue transmission. The available evidence does not justify concluding that persistent Aedes populations or sustained local dengue transmission are established in the city. Standardized longitudinal entomological surveillance, integrated epidemiological and laboratory monitoring, environmental assessment, and coordinated public health preparedness are warranted to reduce uncertainty and facilitate early detection of potential dengue emergence.

articles.titulo: Blends of Furanosesquiterpenes from: An Alternative Strategy for Mosquito Control.
articles.autores: Trebaiocchi G, Spinozzi E, … Petrelli R (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The recent outbreak of vector-borne diseases has highlighted the crucial importance of effective mosquito control programs. Nevertheless, mosquito management still represents a challenge due to the rapid onset of resistance to conventional insecticides. In this regard, there is an increasing research interest in botanicals as attracting valuable sources of insecticidal compounds. Smyrnium olusatrum L. (Apiaceae), an aromatic plant of great scientific relevance, owes its bioactivity to furanosesquiterpenes, whose major constituents include isofuranodiene (IFD), curzerene, 1-β-acetoxyfuranoeudesm-4(15)-ene, and atractylon. Since these compounds have demonstrated promising larvicidal activity against different mosquito species, in this study they were tested individually and in blends against Culex quinquefasciatus Say larvae, demonstrating the occurrence of synergistic interactions leading to enhanced larvicidal activity. In detail, the blend (1:1) consisting of curzerene and atractylon displayed the highest synergistic action (61.25% mortality), double with respect to that expected (33.75%). Moreover, the pure compounds were tested at their LC50 concentrations against the non-target species Daphnia magna Straus, Chaoborus flavicans Meigen, and Tubifex tubifex Müller, with mortalities from 7.5 to 33.7%. Overall, these findings demonstrate that synergistic furanosesquiterpene blends represent a promising botanical strategy for mosquito control, while minimizing the environmental impact associated with conventional insecticides.

articles.titulo: Detection of previously undescribed seadornavirus-related sequences in Culicoides biting midges collected in Hokkaido, Japan.
articles.autores: Matsumura R, Aboshi AR, … Isawa H (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Culicoides biting midges play an important role as vectors of various viruses and are associated with public and veterinary health concerns worldwide. However, our understanding of the diversity and distribution of RNA viruses associated with Culicoides biting midges remains limited. Therefore, this study used next-generation sequencing to investigate RNA viruses in Culicoides biting midges collected in Hokkaido, Japan in 2023. Consequently, we identified previously undescribed seadornavirus-related sequences in the biting midges. Genetic and molecular phylogenetic analyses indicated that these viral sequences were most closely related to Liao ning virus, which has previously been isolated from mosquitoes in China, Australia, and Japan. The putative seadornavirus was tentatively named Mabiro virus. Our findings not only provide new insights into the diversity and evolutionary relationships of seadornaviruses but also further advance our current understanding of viruses associated with Culicoides biting midges in Japan.

articles.titulo: Progress on Dengue Vaccines: A Comprehensive Review of Current and Emerging Vaccines.
articles.autores: Simon CA, Chua JV, Lyke KE (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The global burden of dengue virus continues to increase, driven by environmental changes, urban growth, and the widespread dissemination of Aedes mosquito vectors. Developing an effective dengue vaccine remains challenging because it must provide long-lasting, balanced immunity against each of the four circulating serotypes without increasing the risk of immune-mediated disease enhancement upon exposure to a different serotype. This review article summarizes current understanding of dengue immunopathogenesis, highlights the limitations of first-generation, live-attenuated vaccines, and explores how preexisting serostatus, efficacy across serotypes, and safety considerations affect vaccine implementation. We also review emerging vaccine platforms, including site-directed attenuation, heterologous prime-boost strategies, and mRNA, DNA, and peptide vaccines. Advances in antigen engineering, together with improved diagnostics and surveillance, will be essential to overcoming existing immunologic and implementation barriers. Ongoing innovation, equitable access, and public trust remain critical to achieving effective global dengue control.

articles.titulo: Biodiversity of mosquito fauna (Diptera: Culicidae) associated with bromeliads in Atlantic Forest fragments in the state of Sergipe, Brazil.
articles.autores: Neves AP, Maia PCR, … La Corte R (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The Culicidae exhibits broad taxonomic diversity and significant ecological importance, especially in phytotelm habitats provided by bromeliads. This study investigated the diversity of mosquitoes associated with bromeliads in two Atlantic Forest fragments in Sergipe State, northeastern Brazil: the Morro do Urubu Environmental Protection Area (Morro do Urubu APA), a more disturbed site, and the Mata do Crasto Private Natural Heritage Reserve (Mata do Crasto RPPN), a more preserved area. Collections were carried out during the rainy season and included 26 groups of epiphytic and terrestrial bromeliads. A total of 2,400 specimens belonging to 21 species were identified, of which 14 represent new records for Sergipe and three likely correspond to species new to science. The genus Culex was the most abundant, particularly the subgenus Microculex, which occurred prominently in both areas, indicating ecological plasticity. Anopheles (Kerteszia) bellator, a potential vector of bromeliad malaria, was recorded for the first time in the state. Sampling was considered sufficient in the APA, whereas the RPPN indicated potential for additional records. Temperature influenced species abundance and richness, highlighting the importance of environmental heterogeneity in structuring mosquito communities. The results indicate that the more disturbed site concentrated species adapted to altered environments, such as Culex pleuristriatus and Aedes albopictus. In contrast, the better-preserved site exhibited greater diversity, including rare and specialized species. These patterns demonstrate that anthropogenic disturbance negatively affects mosquito richness and diversity, favoring opportunistic species.

articles.titulo: Tribological Behaviour of Mg-3Zn-xZr-1Y Alloys for Biomedical Implant Applications.
articles.autores: Brown C, Feyzi M, … Hashemi R (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Magnesium (Mg) alloys are promising biodegradable materials for orthopaedic implants because of their bone-like mechanical properties and biocompatibility. However, their clinical application is limited by rapid degradation, caused by the combined effects of wear and corrosion in physiological environments. Understanding the tribological behaviour of these alloys is essential for improving both the design and performance of medical implants. This paper studies recently developed Mg-3Zn-xZr-1Y alloys with a focus on the influence of zirconium (Zr) additions (0.25-1.00 wt%) on the tribological performance for biomedical applications. The developed alloys were tested under dry and physiological conditions simulated by phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) using a customised reciprocating ball-on-disc tribometer. The normal loads of 6, 17.5 and 30.8 N were selected to mimic a range of typical contact pressures experienced by relevant medical implants. The surface damage of the tested alloys was characterised using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and material loss was determined by confocal microscopy. Volume loss analyses showed that PBS significantly reduced material loss as a result of the lubrication effect and the possible formation of tribochemical films. The effect of Zr content on the material loss was found to be highly coupled with the effect of both normal load and the testing environment. SEM characterisations showed that abrasive wear, primarily ploughing and localised cutting, was the dominant degradation mechanism under dry conditions; whereas, in PBS conditions, the dominant degradation mechanism was found to change from abrasive wear to a combination of moderated abrasive wear and oxidation/corrosion.
